articleTitle: Multi-Chirps Convolution Technique for Range Spectrum Signal Enhancement Based on a 60-GHz MIMO FMCW Radar
abstract: Radar is capable of providing essential distance information for targets. While noise interference is typically present in most indoor or outdoor scenes which makes the target in the range spectrum not obvious or even submerged. In this work, a multi-chirps convolution technique which can improve signal to average noise ratio (SANR) by 14.02dB on average with only two chirps through experiments is proposed based on a 60GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar. The multi-chirps convolution technique (MCCT) can suppress irrelevant noise spectrum and enhances the same frequency signals in the spectrum which is related to target distance information. A series of experiments are carried out in real indoor environment to validate the proposed technique. The experimental results demonstrate that the multi-chirps convolution technique can accurately detect the distance of target and effectively improve SANR.

articleTitle: Switchable Reflective Point Design for Ultrabroadband Microwave Absorber
abstract: This paper presents an effective method for significantly expanding the bandwidth of a microwave absorber. The method is achieved by inserting a special switchable layer into the absorber already designed. This layer reconstructs and modulates the reflective properties of the original lower grounded dielectric layer, thus eliminating the bandwidth limitations imposed by its total reflection points. In addition, the absorption bandwidth can be further extended to below 1 GHz by switching the varactors loaded on the switchable layer. The final measurement results are in good agreement with the simulation, demonstrating a switchable -10 dB absorption bandwidth covering 0.66- 5.89 GHz.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Dual Linearly Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element in X-Band
abstract: In this paper, a dual linearly polarized programmable reflectarray (PRA) element with 1-bit phase reconfigurability is proposed. The PRA element mainly comprises a simple L-shaped metal structure and two PIN diodes. By biasing the two PIN diodes, the 1-bit phase shift can be achieved for dual-linear polarizations. Besides, the insertion loss of the element is better than 2.5 dB from 8.5 GHz to 12 GHz, and the 1-bit phase shift keeps stable within 18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}\pm 20^{\circ}$</tex> from 8 GHz to 11.5 GHz. Additionally, the PRA element is demonstrated to have good angular stability. The proposed 1-bit dual linearly polarized PRA element features simple structures, wide bandwidth, and low power consumption, which have significant applications in radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: A SiGe 92–96 GHz 5-bit Active Phase Shifter for W-Band Phased Arrays
abstract: A 5-bit vector modulator type phase shifter is presented in 0.13-μm SiGe technology for W-band phased arrays. A 90° hybrid is applied to divide the input signal into quadrature. Four orthogonal signals are vector synthesized through VGAs, utilizing current steering technology. Through simulation, the RMS phase error of the proposed phase shifter is 2.59° - 2.85° at 92–96 GHz. The simulated average gain is -0.79-1.69dB, while the RMS gain error is 1.82–1.94 dB. The core part of the circuit occupies an area of 0.64 mm × 0.42 mm.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Dual Polarized Multi-Mode OAM Antenna Array
abstract: A dual-polarized multi-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) microstrip antenna array using differential feeding has been proposed in this paper. The antenna element consists of four radiation patches and four driven patches, with two pairs of differential feeding ports. The symmetry of the antenna structure allows the radiation patches to be shared by the adjacent antenna units in the array, which reducing the overall size of the 2×3 array. By controlling the phase of the feeding ports, the array radiates four kinds of the OAM waves, i.e., the OAM modes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l = +1$</tex> and +2 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> polarization and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l = -1$</tex>, and -2 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> polarization. The simulated results show that the antenna has a bandwidth (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{dd11}\vert < -10$</tex> dB) of 3.4-3.9 GHz (13.7%), and the resulting array has a cross-polarization ratio of 24 dB. Good OAM wave characteristics obtained by the proposed array verify the feasibility of the integrated design of polarization multiplexing and mode multiplexing.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflector Surface Assisted UAV Moving Edge Computing Trajectory Optimization
abstract: Due to the complex urban environment, the communication link between user equipment(UE) and unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) may be blocked. The intelligent reflector surface(IRS) communication environment is proposed to enhance the performance of moving edge computing(MEC) networks for UAV. By optimizing the flight path, the UEs' task data is maximized under the constraint of considering the computing power of the UAV. An atomic orbit search(AOS) algorithm based on Levy flight is proposed to solve the above non-convex problem. Simulation results showed that the improved AOS algorithm significantly improves the system performance.

articleTitle: X-Band Phased Vivaldi Array with Low-Scattering Characteristic
abstract: A low-scattering X-band phased Vivaldi array antenna is proposed in this paper. Absorbing material is employed to reduce the scattering under cross-polarized incident waves. Besides, the impedance matching of the Vivaldi element is improved by the matching layer, and the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) at broadside radiation is below 1.25 in most of X-band which, suggests the antenna can absorb most of co-polarized incident waves. Therefore, the in-band low-scattering characteristic is achieved under arbitrary polarized incident waves. Moreover, the array antenna realizes ±60° beam scanning in both E/H planes in X-band. The low-scattering and wide-angle scanning properties of the proposed antenna are both verified by the measured results in the experiment.

articleTitle: An Analog Automatic-Amplitude Control Circuitry for Ultra-wideband LC VCO in 0.18 µm CMOS
abstract: A stand-alone configurable analog automatic-amplitude control (AAC) circuit is presented for ultra-wideband (UWB) voltage control oscillator (VCO), which helps to keep the UWB VCO at reasonable output amplitude over process, voltage, and temperature (PVT). The proposed architecture of VCO with AAC is designed in 0.18 µm CMOS, and consumes 22 mA from a 3.3-V supply voltage. Transistor-level post-simulated results indicate that the 3.2 – 7 GHz multi-core UWB LC VCO is capable of providing the phase noise performance of −124 and −119 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset from 3.2 GHz and 7 GHz carrier, respectively. The variation coefficient of the output single-ended amplitude is no more than 4.5% in all various circumstances, and it hardly worsens phase noise to VCO. One of the attractive points to emerge from the proposed UWB VCO is that the response time could save 40% over traditional architecture, and it could be widely used in other symmetrical/differential types.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle End-Fire Multibeam Metantenna Employing Dual-Layer SIW 9×9 Butler Matrix for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: A wide-angle end-fire metantenna fed by a novel dual-layer substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) 9×9 Butler Matrix (BM) suitable for millimeter-wave applications is proposed in this paper. By introducing a newly-designed dual-layer SIW 9×9 BM and a wide-beamwidth end-fire metantenna, the half-power angular coverage of the proposed multibeam metantenna is up to ±100°. Compared with other similar works, the proposed multibeam metantenna exhibits wide-angle coverage, making it an attractive candidate for 5G millimeter-wave systems.

articleTitle: Broadband Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna with High Suppression in Second Harmonic Frequency
abstract: This manuscript presents a 45° single-polarized magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna with a broad band and high suppression in second harmonic frequency, moreover, no extra filtering circuit is required. The ME dipole is composed of several shorted pins and four rectangular patches, and it is excited by a slot. By adopting a H-shaped slot and bat-shaped stripline, it can realize a broad band and stable gain in the passband. In order to obtain a high suppression in second harmonic frequency, a shorted strip, a stub and a split resonant loop are adopted inside the dipole to introduce two radiation nulls to enhance the suppression in second harmonic frequency. It has weak interference on pass-band and doesn't increase the size of ME dipole. As a result, the antenna exhibits a broad band working in C-band and X-band from 6 to 10.8GHz, and the average gain is 5.5dBi. The harmonic suppression level can be up to 17dB from 17 to 21GHz and the efficiency is suppressed to less than 7%. These results reveal that the proposed antenna without extra filtering circuit can not only work in a wide band, but also have a high harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: Planar Structure-Shared Antenna Using Microstrip Patch and Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity-Backed Monopulse Slot Array
abstract: In this paper, a planar structure-shared antenna is designed with compact size and high channel isolation. And the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed monopulse slot array (CBMSA) is used to replace the microstrip patch, which operate in X- and L-band, respectively. Characteristic mode analysis is applied to insightfully design new microstrip patch antenna with the feed structures of SIW CBMSA. This structure-shared configuration features high channel isolation with about 90 dB at the low frequency and 35 dB at the high frequency, which is because: 1) The radiation mode of SIW slot is much higher than the fundamental mode of new microstrip patch; 2) the coaxial lines of feed structures penetrate through the substrate of the microstrip patch, directly connected to the SIW CBMSA; 3) an isolator layer is added on the top. The SIW CBSMA is realized with boresight gain of sum beam pattern being 13.3 dBi and the null depth of difference beam pattern being 25.3 dB (Z-axis gain is -12 dBi).

articleTitle: A Compact Contactless Waveguide Band-pass Filter for High Sensitivity Passive Intermodulation Measurement
abstract: Passive intermodulation (PIM) is a kind of nonlinear intermodulation products generated in microwave passive components and has harmful impact on microwave communication systems. High sensitivity measurement is essential to accurately evaluate the PIM performance of microwave products. In this work, a low PIM iris waveguide band pass filter (BPF) is proposed for high sensitivity PIM measurement applications. Contactless electromagnetic band gap (EBG) is innovatively utilized to suppress the PIM caused by metallic contact nonlinearity. Furthermore, slow wave waveguide structure is designed to reduce the size of the BPF. A Ku band prototype of the proposed BPF is designed and manufactured, achieving a stable low PIM level with an average PIM suppression more than 20dB compared with traditional BPF, while the size is reduced by more than 40% by slow wave design.

articleTitle: Advanced EM Topology Optimization of the Symmetrical Two-pole Waveguide Filter Using Matrix Dimensionality Reduction Technique
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) topology optimization is a methodology to optimize the EM response of the microwave component by modifying its topology layout. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is among typical algorithms. Matrix Padé Via Lanczos (MPVL) is often applied to accelerate finite element method (FEM) based EM simulations. This paper has optimized a symmetrical two-pole waveguide filter by an efficient topology optimization with GA. A matrix dimensionality reduction technique is applied to fasten the EM simulation in optimization.

articleTitle: A Design of Dual-Polarized 3-D Pattern Manipulation Structure Using Slotline-Based Elements
abstract: A design of dual-polarized 3-D pattern manipulation structure (DP 3-D PMS) using slotline-based elements is presented for future 6G wireless networks. Firstly, the 3-D slotline element with variable slotline length is analyzed. Using this type of element, a single-polarized PMS is realized to control the reflected wave. Then, the expansion of dual-polarized PMS is obtained by utilizing dual-polarized elements with slotline pairs. Finally, calculations and simulations agree well with each other, showing that the proposed DP 3-D PMS possesses the ability to effectively manipulate the reflected wave within an angle range of 45°.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Outphaisng Power Amplifier Based on Multi-Topology Fitting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual-band outphasing power amplifier (OPA) using a new method based on multiple topology fitting based on non-commensurate transmission lines (NCTLs) and extended transmission lines (ETLs). The proposed method enables flexible and efficient design of dual-band OPA by fitting the electrical lengths and characteristic impedance of each branch network at both bands. An OPA prototype operating at 2.6 and 3.5 GHz was fabricated using two 10W GaN HEMT transistors to verify the concept. Test results show that the realized power amplifier achieves maximum output power of 44.4 and 44.3 dBm and peak drain efficiencies of 69.5% and 69.2% at these two bands. The corresponding efficiencies of 62.4% and 63.5% are obtained at the 6-dB power back-off points, respectively.

articleTitle: A Broadband Millimeter-Wave Filtering Antenna with Flat Gain Based on ISGW
abstract: This paper proposes a filtering antenna operating in the millimeter-wave frequency band, which utilizes integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW) technology for feeding. Firstly, to generate a high-frequency radiation null, multiple coupling paths are created from the feeding port to the radiation patch. Secondly, by introducing current nulls through slots on the main radiation patch, a low-frequency radiation null is achieved. Additionally, ISGW can suppress undesired modes and ensure the transmission of the quasi-TEM mode stably. Simulation results show that the filtering antenna has a bandwidth of 17.1% from 25.1 GHz to 29.8 GHz, achieving an average realized gain of 7.4 dBi within the band. The proposed filtering antenna generates a radiation null at 23.6 and 30.8 GHz, respectively, and the gain curve is flat within the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 60–64 GHz Power Amplifier for MM-Wave Radar Transceiver with 16.51-dBm Power and 23.34% PAE in 40-NM CMOS
abstract: A 60–64 GHz high-efficiency CMOS power amplifier (PA) based on a magnetically coupled resonator (MCR) matching network is presented. A design rule for the MCR matching network is proposed, which greatly increases the efficiency and saturated output power. With lower power devices, a two-stage differential PA with neutralized common-source stages has been realized in a 40-nm bulk CMOS process. Simulated in 40-nm CMOS, 23.34% peak power added efficiency (PAE), 16.51-dBm saturated output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{\text{sat}})$</tex>, 15.81-dB power gain, and 12.54- dBm output 1-dB compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{1\text{dB}})$</tex> with 11.18% PAE are achieved by the proposed P A chip at 60 GHz. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\text{sat}}$</tex> is above 16.2-dBm, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_{1\text{dB}}$</tex> is above 11.6-dBm and the peak PAE is above 20% across the 60–64 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Inhibition Multipactor Method of High Power Ferrite Circulator for Aerospace
abstract: In order to meet requirements of high power, low loss and high isolation of the satellite payload high-power ferrite circulator, the waveguide juction circulator is used in the space application environment. Multi-stage matching was adopted to achieve the bandwidth and isolation requirements. In the impedance matching of the multipactor sensitive region of the loop, the slope structure was adopted to meet inhibition multipactor. In S-band, the work bandwidth is more than 10%, input port standing wave ratio little than 1.15, and isolation bigger than 25 dB. Then, the threshold of simulation and test about multipactor for this ferrite circulator is more than 10 kW with peak power and 1% duty of cycle, that can be used for space payload for inhibotion multipactor.

articleTitle: Study on Packaging of a Wideband Filtering Out-of-Phase Power Divider Based on Multi-Layer Stacked Striplines
abstract: This paper presents a compact design method for out-of-phase power divider with wideband filtering response and high isolation based on multi-layer stacked striplines. By modifying the input transmission line (TL) in a traditional Marchand balun as a one-wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda_{\mathrm{g}})$</tex> short-circuited one, out-of-phase power division with a three-pole high selective filtering response is obtained. Based on the advantages of stripline, broadside coupling is adopted so that required coupling strength for wideband performance can be achieved. Then, a grounded resistor is loaded via a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}/2$</tex> TL between two output ports, leading to a high isolation over the wide passband. Finally, an example circuit centered at 2 GHz is designed by utilizing multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB) and packaged by multiple screws. The realized circuit size is only about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.14\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}\times 0.13\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}\times 0.02\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}\text{mm}^{3}s$</tex>. To verify the reliability of proposed packaging design method, both simulated and measured results are displayed and good agreement in the working passband is found.

articleTitle: Short-time Heart Rate Estimation Based on 60-GHz FMCW Radar
abstract: A short-time non-contact heart rate estimation method based on a commercial 60GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) millimeter-wave radar is proposed in this work. The proposed approach involves the use of the average elimination method to suppress background noise and the median filtering to eliminate impulse noise interference. More importantly, the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise analysis (ICEEMDAN) and the fast independent component analysis (Fast-ICA) are jointly used to suppress respiratory harmonics so that the signal-to-noise ratio of heartbeat signal is increased; meanwhile, the estimation is also speeded up since the numbers of pseudo modes and iterations are reduced. Experiments show that the proposed method can achieve fast heart rate estimation with mean absolute errors less than 4 beats per minute (BPM) over short durations of 5-second.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Characteristics of Near-field Coherent Sensing for Cardiac Monitoring
abstract: The near-field coherent sensing (NCS) method can couple significant electromagnetic energy to the sensing area and detect weak scattering signals inside the human body. To explore the detecting resolution, the CST simulation is implemented to calculate the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) along with the distance between the target and interference source. Moreover, according to the simulation results, heartbeat extraction experiments are carried out. The results show that two points with a distance of 6.5 cm at 1 GHz can be clearly distinguished.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method to Extract Properties of Periodic Slow Wave Structures for TWT Applications
abstract: In this paper, a new two-step method is proposed to extract the characteristic properties of periodic slow-wave structures (SWS). The SOL calibration technique is used to eliminate the influence of error boxes at both ends of the circuit to obtain the transmission matrix of the core circuit. Then the characteristic properties including the complex propagation constant and the complex characteristic impedance are calculated. Following the calculation process of the proposed method, a co-planar slow-wave structure is studied in the paper as an example to verify the effectiveness of the method. Further, the input-output coupler is thereby designed based on the calculated results. The corresponding impedance matching is quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Electromagnetic Effect of the EAT Screen on the Localizer Antenna and Glide-Slope Localizer Antenna in the Airport
abstract: The electromagnetic environment in airport is very complex. glide-slope localizer and localizer are part of the Instrument Landing System. They cooperate with the airborne receiver to provide space guidance for the aircraft during the approach and landing process. The End-around Taxiway Screen built at the end of the airport runway will cause interference to the electromagnetic environment of the airport and have a certain impact on the aircraft approach and landing process. In this paper, the model of glide-slope localizer and localizer antenna array and the model of visual shield are established. The coupling effect of End-around Taxiway Screen (EAT Screen) and localizer antenna array is analyzed by image method. The hybrid simulation method of finite element and bouncing ray method is used to improve the simulation efficiency, which provides technical methods for the research of civil aviation electromagnetic compatibility and can provide support for the planning and construction of End-Around Taxiway Screen.

articleTitle: Multi-Transmitter Coils Optimization for Range-Adaptive Wireless Power Transfer by Using Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a design method for a multi-transmitter wireless power transfer (WPT) system that aims to achieve stable and high-power transfer efficiency (PTE) across a wide range. The proposed method utilizes a Genetic algorithm (GA) to obtain the parameters of three transmitter coils that can cope with different distances. Experimental results demonstrate that the presented 3-transmitter coils outperform the conventional transmitting coil, especially in scenarios where the WPT system operates under misalignment and over longer distances. Even when the receiving coil is moved within a distance range of 30-130mm and an offset range of 0-130mm, the PTE of the system remains above 70% throughout the entire range.

articleTitle: Miniaturized, Low Loss Bandpass Filters Based on SISL Technology with Improved Stopband Rejection
abstract: In this paper, a self-packaged bandpass filter (BPF) based on substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) technology platform is proposed. The BPF is designed by using two quarter- wavelength stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) and one half- wavelength SIR. Three transmission zeros (TZs) at the upper and lower sidebands of the passband are introduced by the mixed coupling between resonators. By loading a capacitor in the half- wavelength SIR, improved suppression at the upper sideband is realized. The implemented BPF, featured with self packaging and a compact size of 0.34 is the guided wavelength at 6 GHz), achieves a low insertion loss (IL) of only 0.58 dB and fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 47.4%.

articleTitle: On-Chip Wideband Bandpass Filter with High Frequency Selectivity and Low Insertion Loss Based on GaAs Integrated Passive Device Technology
abstract: In this paper, an on-chip wideband bandpass filter (BPF) with high frequency selectivity and low insertion loss is proposed using gallium arsenide (GaAs) integrated passive device (IPD) technology. Multiple transmission zeros can be provided by the capacitors loaded on the series and parallel LC resonators for the proposed design. Comparing with the state-of-the-art on-chip wideband BPFs, the proposed design has the advantages of high frequency selectivity and low loss. The final filter centered at 1.93 GHz with the 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 64.2% is demonstrated, which exhibits the excellent shape factor (30-dB BW/3-dB BW) of 1.28 and the minimum insertion loss of 1.17 dB.

articleTitle: An X-band GaN HEMT High-Efficiency Switchless Class-G Power Amplifier
abstract: This paper introduces an X-band switchless class-G (SLCG) power amplifier fabricated in 0.15-µm GaN HEMT technology. The switchless Class-G is adopted to improve the output back-off efficiency without additional bandwidth limitation. The measurement results in 8.2-9.2 GHz show that the PA achieves a maximum output power of 37.2 dBm and an average power-added efficiency of 22% at the 6-dB output back-off. The ACPR after digital pre-distortion is better than -48 dBc for a 20MHz long-term evolution (LTE) signal with a 7.5 dB PAPR.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Coding Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array for Two-Dimensional Wide-Angle Beam-Scanning
abstract: We present a 1-bit coding array using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> cylindrical dielectric resonator antennas (CDRAs) designed at 2.45 GHz for two-dimensional (2D) beam-scanning. By symmetrically exciting the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$HE_{11\delta}$</tex> mode of a CDRA, a 180° radiation phase difference is obtained, resulting in a 1-bit characteristic. The excited probe is selected by a switchable feeding and is controlled by a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). A series-parallel hybrid microstrip feeding network is deployed for introducing an initial gradient phase distribution to the array and therefore suppressing the inherent symmetrical grating lobe when 1-bit phase resolution is adopted. By designing the coding patterns, the single beam CDRA array can reach a scanning coverage with a ± 50° elevation angle range and 360° azimuth angle range under 3dBi gain fluctuation. The proposed CDRA array is fabricated and measured, and the simulated and measured results are in a good agreement. The proposed array featuring low-cost and low profile is suitable for terminals to interact with continuously moving communication platforms.

articleTitle: A Flexible and Wearable All-Fabric Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: An entirely fabric-based rectenna is presented in this research. The flexible and wearable rectenna exhibits the characteristics of compact structure, simple manufacturing and excellent energy conversion efficiency over a broad power range. The flexible rectangular patch antenna and flexible voltage doubler rectifying circuit process impedance matching bandwidths of 1.61GHz - 1.65GHz and 1.47GHz - 1.77GHz, respectively. Meanwhile, the fabric-based rectifier can achieve an RF-to-de conversion efficiency better than 40% at OdBm - 15dBm RF incident power when operating at 1.64GHz, and the maximum energy conversion efficiency is 48.27% at 10dBm incident power. The aforementioned results demonstrate that the developed all-fabric rectenna may deliver a trustworthy energy source and has potential applications in wearable self-powered electronic devices in the Internet of Things era.

articleTitle: Fusion Location Method Based on 5G Carrier Phase
abstract: High-precision positioning for 5G mobile terminals is still difficult. This paper studies the positioning algorithm of fusion carrier phase measurement technology and Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA). Low precision distance is measured by TDOA. The carrier phase of received signals from multiple BSs are used for high-precision positioning and the carrier phase integer ambiguity is determined according to this distance to further improve positioning accuracy. An experimental system is built with the Software Defined Radio (SDR) to evaluate the positioning accuracy of this method. The test results show that when the positioning error of TDOA is less than 14cm, the positioning error in the experimental environment in this paper can be further reduced to less than 1cm.

articleTitle: A 5.8-GHz GaN-Based Rectifier with High Power and High Efficiency
abstract: In this paper, a high-power rectifier based on gallium nitride (GaN) Schottky barrier diode is proposed for wireless power transmission (WPT) at 5.8 GHz. Firstly, a tri-bridge structured patterned Schottky diode is designed and fabricated. The small series resistance (1.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega)$</tex> and low turn-on voltage (0.49V) are advantageous for reducing power losses, while the high breakdown voltage (50 V) is designed to cope with high-power scenarios. Subsequently, a high-efficiency and wide-band single-series rectifier operating at 5.8 GHz is proposed. The load resistance is intentionally optimized to 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> to enhance the current driving capability of the rectifier. Measurements show that a maximum conversion efficiency of 72.4% is achieved at an input power of 33.4dBm, resulting in a DC voltage of 12.59V (current of 125.9mA). The rectifier achieves an efficiency over 60% in the power range of 25dBm to 35dBm and indicates the potential to provide energy for high-power devices such as electric vehicles.

articleTitle: 3D Slice Imaging of Non-Line-of-Sight Targets with Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: In this paper, three-dimensional (3D) slice imaging of non-line-of-sight targets with a millimeter wave radar is demonstrated. In the demonstrated system, a low-cost, fully integrated AWR1843 millimeter-wave radar driven by a roller is used to scan the imaging area, and near-filed imaging of hidden targets with different positions and shapes is achieved. The influence of radar bandwidth on imaging quality is studied by comparing the images acquired under different radar bandwidths. The results show that with the increase of the radar bandwidth, clarity of the image is significantly improved, and the speckle effect around the target is also suppressed remarkably, which provides a reliable basis for achieving high-quality images with millimeter wave radars.

articleTitle: Weak Nonlinear Behavioral Model Extraction Based on Vector Network Analyzer
abstract: For the radio frequency and microwave receiver, it mostly works in the linear region or weak nonlinear region. Since multiple filters are used in the chain, only the fundamental characteristics of the chain should be considered. So a vector network analyzer (VNA) is usually used to test the receiver front-end. However, the obtained S-parameters cannot characterize the nonlinear effects of the receiver. In this paper, a VNA will be used to test the power-dependent S-parameters, and after data processing, the S2D nonlinear behavioral model will be extracted. Using the S2D model, the weak nonlinear effects of the receiver front-end can be characterized cheaply and efficiently.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized SISL Bandstop Filter with High Rejection Based on Dual-Mode Resonator
abstract: A miniaturized substrate integrated suspend line (SISL) bandstop filter with high attenuation is proposed in this paper. To realize a higher rejection level, a novel dual-mode resonator is proposed and studied. The dual-mode resonator achieves large capacitance to ground and coupling with the transmission line, which enables the notch filter to achieve high performance while achieving miniaturization. In addition, the proposed dual-mode resonator can realize the high-order bandstop rejection conveniently by series connecting the resonators. To verify the proposed theory, a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order bandstop filter was designed, fabricated, and tested. Measured results agree well with simulated data.

articleTitle: Beyond Field-of-View Detection Based on FMCW Radar Multi-Path Effect in Consumer Applications
abstract: The integration of Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave FMCW radar technology into consumer applications is becoming increasingly prevalent in our daily lives. The Field of View (FoV) of the FMCW radar is usually limited, which constrains its application in consumer scenarios. On the other hand, the complexity of consumer scenarios frequently leads to the presence of multipath effects, which are commonly perceived as a challenge to be addressed. In this work, based on the multipath effect of FMCW radar, a radio channel model for beyond FoV Detection is established. The theory and working principle are presented. Experiments carried out in the office environment show that the subject person's vital signs and body movements were detected when the subject person sat outside of the radar FoV.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Second-Order Balanced Bandpass Filter with Differential-and Common-Mode Two-Port-Quasi-Reflectionless Behavior
abstract: A second-order balanced bandpass filter (BPF) with both differential-mode (DM) and common-mode (CM) two-port-quasi-reflectionless characteristics is reported. It consists of two multi-layer wideband magic-Ts, which are back-to-back connect-ed by means of a symmetrical-quasi-reflectionless complemen-tary-diplexer-based second-order narrow-band BPF, whose out-put ports are designed as balanced input/output terminals of the overall BPF device. By means of the conceived filter topology, an enlarged DM power-absorption spectral range and an enhanced DM passband flatness are attained. On the other hand, by loading two lossy multi-section microstrip lines at the ∑ ports of the used magic-Ton microstrip-to-slotline transitions, a broadband CM quasi-reflectionless response is featured for the devised BPF. These characteristics make the proposed configuration unique, as most of previously-reported balanced BPFs focus on only CM or DM RF -power absorption. For experimental-validation purposes, a two-layer balanced BPF prototype at 2 GHz with DM and CM two-port-quasi-reflectionless capabilities is built and tested. It exhibits a high-selectivity/enhanced-passband-flatness DM filtering response with 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 12.3%, along with minimum DM and CM RF-power-absorption levels of 10 dB from 0.96 to 3.14 GHz (i.e., 3.27:1 spectral ratio) and from 0.96 to 3.33 GHz (i.e., 3.47:1 spectral ratio), respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of Q/W -band Beacons System for GEO Communication Satellite
abstract: The Q-band and W-band of electromagnetic wave have broadband which have significant advantages for satellite-ground communication. However, it also encounters many difficulties and challenges by adapting Q-band and W-band to communication in technique, such as propagation influenced by climate. To deal with the problems, the development of a Q/W dual-band beacon system is introduced which is installed on board of a GEO communication satellite. The beacon system is used to test the characterization of Q-band and W-band satellite-ground propagation channel, including research on atmospheric attenuation and rainfall attenuation.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Sleep Apnea Detection System Based on Data-Driven Methods Using FMCW Radar
abstract: Sleep apnea is a prevalent and serious sleep disorder. Conventional diagnostic methods mainly rely on contact sensors, which are inconvenient and uncomfortable. Radar-based non-contact sleep monitoring overcomes these drawbacks and can serve as an effective alternative. This paper proposes a non-contact sleep apnea detection system based on FMCW radar using machine learning. Feature extraction and deep learning methods established the correlation between respiratory signals and abnormal events. The feature-based approach achieved 88.42% accuracy, 0.8700 sensitivity, 0.8935 specificity, and 0.7592 Kappa in 23 clinical data cases.

articleTitle: Experiment Validation of Multiple Radar Waveform Generation using Time-Domain Coding Digital Metasurface
abstract: In this paper, a time-domain coding digital metasurface (TDCM) is proposed to generate radar waveforms through experiments. In traditional radar systems, radar waveform generation requires radio-frequency (RF) circuits to shift baseband signal to RF frequency, which is complicated, costly, and hard to integrate with transmitting antennas. With the ability to control the frequency spectra of electromagnetic waves in real time, the TDCM makes it possible to generate radar waveforms without RF circuits. During the experimental validation, a TDCM was used to generate four kinds of radar waveforms, indicating it has the potential to redefine the radar architecture in the future.

articleTitle: Decoupling Between Two Closely Spaced Asymmetric Microstrip Patch Antenna by Mode Cancellation Method
abstract: In this paper, a pair of asymmetrically coupled microstrip patch antennas working at 2.45 GHz are proposed. The proposed antenna has been designed using the mode cancellation theory for both common mode (CM) and differential mode (DM). The proposed antenna is self-decoupled by simply inserting a lumped inductance between the two antennas to adjust the differential mode impedance, and no additional decoupled structure is required. The simulation results show that the -10 dB band-width of the proposed antenna is 2.42 GHz ~2.49 GHz, and the isolation is improved greatly from 8.8 dB to 19.5 dB. Compared with the existing research, this design studies the self-decoupling of asymmetric antenna, and has a simple structure, which has a possesses promising potential in MIMO antenna array.

articleTitle: A Reusable Interposer for Multi-Chiplet Microsystems Reconfiguration
abstract: The advantages of Chiplet cannot be fully exploited in the microsystem for the lack of reconfiguration technology. A reusable interposer is proposed for the functional reconfiguration of multi-Chiplet microsystems, which is integrated with a signal routing Chiplet for dynamically adjusting the path between Chiplets and 3D heterogeneous interconnection (TSV and RDL) for signal transmission. The signal routing Chiplet is analyzed with an ABCD matrix. The insertion loss is less than 5 dB and isolation is greater than 45 dB from DC to 8 GHz. The interposer has huge potential for microsystem reconfiguration and miniaturization.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Plasma Limiter Using the SETD method with a Multi-Physics Model
abstract: The plasma limiter can reflect and absorb the high-power microwave to protect the electronic systems. In this paper, a coupled multi-physics model based on the wave equation and electron hydrodynamic equation is proposed and the response properties of the plasma limiter under high power microwave radiation are analyzed using the spectral element time domain (SETD) method. The superiority of the transient fully coupled analysis under high power microwaves is demonstrated by comparison with COMSOL.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Fingerprint Extraction and Identification for Wi-Fi Signals in Noisy Channels
abstract: A noise-robust radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) extraction and identification scheme is proposed and demonstrated for Wi-Fi device recognition. Specifically, an RFF extractor pre-trained by supervised contrastive learning extracts the distinctive features from the spectrogram, which is produced by Fourier-based sychrosqueezing transform (FSST). Then a neural network-based classifier is adopted for precise device identification with the extracted RFF. Utilizing 11 commercial wireless network interface controllers (WNICs), the experimental results demonstrate the significant performance improvement for noisy channels, with classification accuracy achieving up to 95.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 86% when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is 10 and 5 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Low-profile and Ultra-wideband Monocone Antenna with Shorted Top Hat Based on A Concave Curve
abstract: This manuscript presents a monocone antenna with the merits of ultra-wideband and low profile for wireless communication applications. Firstly, a curve, which is determined by the formula given by an exponential function, is used to express the side surface profile of the monocone antenna. And the parameters of the formula of the curve are analyzed in order to improve impedance matching of the antenna at higher frequency band. Furthermore, four shorting pins and a top hat etched with a ring slot and eight circular arc slots are loaded to move the working band towards lower band, then the band is further widened. The simulated results reveal that the proposed monocone antenna with a small height of only 0.06 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> low can cover a very large band from 1.8 to 23.5 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 171.5% for VSWR less than 2.5. The antenna also maintains the gain of 2 dBi to 7 dBi over the whole frequency band. Compared with other antennas of the same height, the antenna can cover a larger bandwidth.

articleTitle: Wideband Metamaterial Crossed-Arm Unit Cell for the Design of Beam-Scanning Circularly Polarized Reflectarray Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable metamaterial unit cell using crossed arms and its application in designing a wideband beam-scanning circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray (RA) antenna. The unit cell is comprised of two pairs of reconfigurable rotated crossed-arms. One pair is connected by two line strips, and the other pair is connected by two arc-shaped strips. The unit cell is verified with a broad CP reflection bandwidth of 7.7-15.5 GHz. An equivalent circuit is utilized to illustrate its working principle for wide CP reflection bandwidth. Based on this meta material unit cell, a broadband RA antenna was designed, developed, and tested for the initial CP performance verification. A high gain of 26.3 dBic with the maximum aperture efficiency of 58.3 % is obtained for this fabricated RA antenna. In addition, a broad CP bandwidth (from 7.6 GHz to 15.9 GHz) for axial ratio <3 dB is achieved for the high gain unidirectional CP radiation.

articleTitle: A 1.2V Low-Power Multi-Band Mixing Frequency Synthesizer for FDD System
abstract: This article presents a novel low-power multi-band mixing frequency synthesizer for FDD System. The synthesizer can provide local oscillation signals for both TX and RX simultaneously with only one phase-locked loop (PLL). By selecting the spacing frequency between the uplink and downlink as its reference, plus a notch filter removing strong spur component, this PLL achieves lower power consumption and smaller die area. The mixing frequency synthesizer is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS process with an area of 0.571 mm2, The test results show that the proposed synthesizer achieves a 3.3-3.66 GHz frequency tuning range with the out-of-band PN of -114.9 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset from a 3.42 GHz carrier. And the reference spur is measured to be -50.16 dBc at 180 MHz offset. The entire mixing frequency synthesizer consumes 7.2 mW at the 1.2 V supply voltage with 4.15 mW associated with VCO.

articleTitle: Stokes Parameter-Based Object Enhancement in Passive Millimeter-Wave Imaging
abstract: Passive millimeter wave (PMMW) imaging has many applications, and personnel security inspection is one of its important applications. The previous imaging system often only uses a single polarization and so does not take full advantage of the multi-polarization information. In different polarization images, the contrast between local targets and body background is different, and the optimal contrast performance of all local targets cannot be obtained in any single polarized image at the same time. To give full use to the local feature advantages of multiple polarized images, this paper proposes a subregional fusion method for object enhancement using Stokes parameters, which can fuse the optimal local regions in different polarized images, so that the object and body background in the fusion image have the optimal contrast.

articleTitle: A 20.9-nW 32.768-kHz Real-Time Clock with 2.2-ppm Temperature Stability for Outdoor Wireless IoT Application
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low power quartz crystal temperature-compensated real-time clock. By using a pulse injection oscillator (PIO) instead of a conventional Pierce oscillator, a multi-phase output is provided to improve digital compensation accuracy while reducing power consumption. The temperature compensation is achieved by dynamically selecting the multi-phase output of the PIO based on the lookup table data to offset the temperature drift, which improves the instantaneous compensation accuracy compared to the traditional digital frequency division-based method. An on-chip ring oscillator controlled by a proportional to absolute temperature current source using switched capacitor is implemented to obtain temperature information by counting its output frequency. Simulation based on the TSMC 65 nm CMOS process shows that the circuit has an absolute long-term compensation accuracy of 2.2 ppm and a total power consumption of 20.9 nW at typical operating conditions of 25°C and 0.6 V supply.

articleTitle: Miniaturized W-band Bandpass Filter Using IPD Technology
abstract: This work presents the design of a four-order bandpass filter (BPF) for W-band applications using integrated passive device (IPD) technology. A coupling architecture with three configurable transmission zeros is employed to improve the passband selectivity. Additionally, combining folded stub loaded resonators (SLRs) and stacking resonators vertically reduces the overall foot-print of the circuit. The simulation results show that the suggested BPF, which operates at 95 GHz, has a number of benefits including low insertion loss, excellent selectivity, small size, and convenient to be integrated. The compact size and easy integration of the proposed BPF render it a compelling option for upcoming wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Slotted Patch Excited ME Dipole Antenna for Broadband Millimeter Wave and Satellite Applications
abstract: A broadband slotted patch antenna excited Magne-to- Electric dipole (ME-dipole) antenna is proposed in this paper for millimeter wave and satellite communication. The ME-dipole is placed on a coupled-feed cavity-backed slotted patch antenna. The slotted patch antenna acts as both a radiator and a ground for the ME-dipole. By combining the ME-dipole and the slotted patch antenna, a -10dB impedance bandwidth covering over 22.86-44.35 GHz (63.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) is realized. The pattern of the antenna element remains stable throughout this bandwidth. Based on this antenna element, a 4x4 single linearly polarized (LP) array is designed and tested. Measured results show that a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 51.2%, and a peak gain of 20.4 dBi with a 3dB gain bandwidth over 40.6% are realized.

articleTitle: A 0.5-2 GHz Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with Tunable N-Path Filter for Wideband Wireless Application in 40-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a passive mixer-first receiver in 40 nm CMOS process at 0.5-2 GHz for wideband wireless application. In the proposed design, an 8-path full differential passive mixer was adopted in the input, significantly improving the out-of-band-IIP3 (OOB-IIP3) and image rejection (IR) performance. A noise decoupling technology is utilized in the baseband to minimize noise figure (NF). The post-layout simulation results show that the receiver achieves 2.2 dB double-sideband integrated NF, more than 16 dBm OOB-IIP3, and voltage gain over 46 dB with a total power consumption of 49.9 mW, including an 8-phase LO divider with a 3-stage buffer.

articleTitle: A Compact LNA with 23.3 dB Gain and 3.4 dB NF for V-Band Phased Array Systems in 65-nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a compact V-band low noise amplifier (LNA) employed stability enhancement and optimized transformer-based matching technique. The LNA is composed of two pseudo-difference common-source stages structure. Each stage adopts the neutralizing capacitor technology to optimize the noise figure and employ the transformer-matching network for a compact footprint. The proposed LNA is implemented in a 65-nm CMOS technology and consume a DC power of 38 mW at a sup-ply of 1.2 V. The amplifier achieves a 23.3 dB gain with a 3-dB bandwidth between 48.3 and 55.8 GHz. At 52 GHz, the optimum noise figure (NF) is 3.4 dB and is below than 3.65 dB over the whole band. Thanks to the compact transformer-based matching network, the LNA achieves a core chip size of only 0.09 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,

articleTitle: SAW Filter with High Out-of-Band Rejection Using Improved Grounding Method
abstract: A surface acoustic wave (SAW) bandpass filter with high out-of-band rejection is proposed in this paper. An improved grounding configuration is utilized by connecting the ground of the double-mode SAW (DMS) structure and the shunt resonator together. Both of them are connected to the printed circuit board (PCB) through bonding wire. The influence of the parasitic inductance is modeled and studied in detail, which helps to improve the out-of-band rejection and enhances the design flexibility. This filter is fabricated on a standard 42° Y-X Lithium Tantalate (LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) substrate. It has a center frequency of 1085MHz and a fractional bandwidth of 3%. The rejection achieves 40dB on both the left side and right side of the passband. The measured results and the simulated ones are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Microwave-Induced Thermoacoustic Tomography: An Application in Joint Imaging
abstract: The conventional microwave-induced thermoacoustic tomography (TAT) projects the three-dimensional information of a section thickness onto a two-dimensional plane. For joint imaging, the signals of the thin tissue and surrounding bone can be superimposed and projected onto a transducer's scanning plane. Due to the low microwave absorption of the bone, the TAT image of the joint appears dark mottled, resulting in the difficulty of clear and complete reconstruction of some joint tissues. To alleviate this problem, a dual-frequency TAT method was proposed to image the rabbit knee joint and to detect meniscal injury. Compared with the traditional single-frequency TAI images, the corresponding dual-frequency TAI images can more clearly and completely reconstruct various joint tissues and detect joint injury, showing more accurate tissue size and signal trend. Therefore, this method can improve the ability of TAT to image joint tissues, promote the progress of related applications, and also provide a reference for other imaging techniques that are needed to alleviate negative effects of bone.

articleTitle: A 180µW Dynamic Zoom ADC With 110 dB SNDR in 2 kHz BW
abstract: A dynamic zoom analog-to-digital converter(ADC) used in low-voltage and low-power sensor applications related to the Internet of Things(IoT) is presented in this paper. It employs a coarse 5-bit asynchronous successive approximation register(SAR) ADC and a fine second-order delta-sigma modulater(Δ ∑ M). The SAR ADC dynamically updates the references of Δ ∑ M that reduces the loop filter requirements. A low-voltage operational transconductance amplifier(OTA) and a low-power comparator are used in the dynamic zoom ADC. Designed in a 65nm CMOS process, the layout occupies 0.47mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It achieves 110-dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion-ratio(SNDR) in 2-kHz bandwidth(BW), while only consuming 180µW from a 1.1-V supply. This achieves a Schreier figure of merit(FoM) of 181 dB.

articleTitle: Annulus-Shaped ±45°-Polarized Antenna With Broad Band and Enhanced Gain and Isolation
abstract: A high-gain, high isolation, and broadband design of ±45°dual-polarized antenna is presented. It starts from a simpler single-polarized printed circuit board (PCB) dipole antenna with a pair of 1/4 wavelength arms and a ~1/4 wavelength balun. The arms of the dipole antenna are then curved into a 1/4 circular arc-alike patch, and four dipole antennas are joined, end to end and with gaps between each other, to make an annulus-shaped radiation aperture with a pair of +45°-polarized dipoles and a pair of -45°-polarized dipoles. Finally, both +45°-pair and -45°-pair are, individually, merged into a +45°-port and a -45°-port of the proposed antenna through a micro-strip combiner on top side of the bedframe. Besides, the choke technique is also employed in this design to ensure low cross-band scattering in multi-band and multi-array applications. Over a broad working band of 698–960 MHz this design achieves VSWR < 1.5, gain of 9.5-11.3 dBi, and well isolation of > 26 dB.

articleTitle: High Gain Series-Fed Patch Antenna for Anti-Collision Automotive Radar
abstract: This paper presents a 77GHz high-gain series-fed anti-collision antenna for autonomous vehicles. The designed antenna comprises a series-fed array of 10 patches and a cap-shaped fin structure fed by a coplanar waveguide structure. The designed antenna can operate in the impedance bandwidth of 76.19-77.82GHz, meeting the working band of 77GHz automotive anti-collision radar. Good impedance matching with a reflection coefficient of lower than −10 dB and stable and symmetrical radiation with a high gain of 15 – 20 dBi at 76.19-77.82GHz is obtained. The antenna's performance is suitable for applying 77GHz anti-collision radar for vehicles.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Antenna Using Metasurface for 5G Application
abstract: A dual-band and dual-polarized antenna using metasurface for 5G application is proposed in this paper. The antenna has achieved excellent dual-band broadside radiation performance maintaining a low profile characteristic by introducing a dual-layer metasurface structure. The bandwidths of the proposed antenna are 13.9% (2.46-2.83GHz) and 14.4% (3.22-3.72GHz), whose overall size is 0.82λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.82λ <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.053λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. For these dual operating bands, the antenna achieves high realized gains of 8.4-9.88dBi and 9.12-11.85dBi, respectively, with interport isolation over 40dB.

articleTitle: Design of ISGW Unequal Power Divider Based on Ultra-Wideband Metamaterial Absorber
abstract: This paper presents an effective method based on the concept of indium tin oxide (ITO) films designed metamaterial absorber to achieve unequal power divider. The structural unit of the proposed metamaterial absorber consists of three films, a foam dielectric substrate and a metallic copper. By properly adjusting the resonance of the structure, an optimized metamaterial absorption rate of greater than 90% from 21 to 35 GHz is achieved, and a strong absorption effect of ultra-broadband for incident electromagnetic waves at different polarization angles and different incidence angles is achieved, which is in good agreement with the numerical simulation results, and an equivalent circuit model is extracted to explain its operation mechanism. The designed metamaterial is loaded on an Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide (ISGW) based power divider. Simulation results show that the 4:1 unequal power divider achieves a relative bandwidth of 24% in the operating band 22–28 GHz, and the isolation is better than 15dB, and the return loss is greater than 10dB.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Shared-Aperture Antenna for Satellite Communication Applications
abstract: A millimeter-wave dual-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna for satellite communication applications is proposed in this study. A low-band (LB) dielectric resonator element is placed on top of a high-band (HB) patch element in the proposed antenna. The LB unit's radiator uses a non-metallic cube dielectric resonator to minimize the impact of LB elements on HB element radiation performance, allowing radiation from HB elements to flow through LB elements without degradation. A dual-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna working at 25.87-28.09 GHz (LB) and 28.44-32.07 GHz (HB) is constructed and simulated. The proposed antenna has a lower profile coverage of only 1.143 mm (0.103 λ <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, λ <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the working wavelength at the center frequency of LB).

articleTitle: Design of On-Chip Ultra-Miniaturized Low-Loss Dual-Band Bandpass Filter in LTCC for 5G Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel on-chip ultra-miniaturized dualband bandpass filter (D-BPF) using the low-temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) technology is proposed. To realize the ultra-miniaturization of the proposed D-BPF, the vertical configuration for the lower and upper bands is implemented. The low insertion loss and wide passbands can be obtained by using direct coupling between resonators. Furthermore, the simplified LC model of the proposed layout is given and analyzed. For verification, the proposed DBPF is designed, simulated, fabricated and measured, respectively. Finally, the D-BPF used in the sub-6 GHz band with the core size of 3.3 mm × 2.8 mm can cover from 3.01 to 3.79 GHz and from 4.77 to 5.33 GHz within the condition of │S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>│ < -15 dB.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Terahertz Imaging Based on Sparse Multistatic Linear Array
abstract: Imaging with a sparse multistatic linear array can overcome the limitations of traditional scanning three-dimensional (3D) terahertz (THz) imaging systems, which require time-consuming measurement procedures and limit their potential for industrial applications. This paper discusses the implementation of a THz 3D imaging system based on a sparse multistatic linear array. The sparse linear array operates within the frequency range of 170GHz to 210GHz and is combined with a conveying device to realize a synthetic aperture. The high-speed electronic scanning and multi-channel synchronous reception of the conveying device enables scanning tests to be performed at a speed of 20 cm/s. 3D images can be reconstructed using the back-projection algorithm. The system design, including the array design and data processing algorithms, is presented, and the 3D imaging performance of the system is verified using experimental results.

articleTitle: UAV Swarm Cooperative Penetration Electronic Countermeasures Technology Modeling and Application
abstract: Understanding and mastering the composition and characteristics of UAV swarm penetration jamming technology is the basis for conducting anti-jamming research of air defense and anti-missile system. In view of the complexity of the air defense system environment, the main jamming measures adopted at different stages are analyzed according to the flight process of UAV. Based on the anti-jamming technology characteristics of modern air defense system, the modeling methods of noise frequency modulation, frequency shift coverage noise suppression, joint false track deception and other jamming technologies are studied. Through research, it lays a foundation for in-depth evaluation of UAV swarm penetration jamming effectiveness, and has important application value for improving UAV swarm combat capability in complex confrontation environment.

articleTitle: Optimal Wave Field States in Disordered Environments Based on Electromagnetic Information Theory
abstract: On-demand wave field control is the key goal of wave field research, but the optimal wave field states in disordered environments are always a difficult problem. The electromagnetic information theory (EMIT) is naturally suitable to solve this problem because it takes the disordered environments into account. Here, we classify disordered environments into known and unknown categories. For the known disordered environments, we use the group T-matrix method and information mode decomposition method to get the optimal wave field states. For unknown disordered environment, we use a non-iterative operator to characterize the properties of scatters, called the D operator based on the EMIT. To further demonstrate the feasibility, we give a control method to realize these optimal wave field states. Our theory will be widely used in many promising applications, such as on-demand communication, adaptive focusing, and microforce sensing.

articleTitle: Modular Neural Network for Coupled-Resonator Filter Modeling with EM-Sensitivity
abstract: This paper presents a study on the neural network-based surrogate modeling of coupled-resonator microwave filters. The proposed model consists of several modules that are constructed independently to form a modular neural network. To ensure the accuracy of the neural network model across a wide range of training data, electromagnetic (EM) sensitivity is exploited. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, a 6–2 dielectric filter design is tested.

articleTitle: Analysis Method for Estimating Transfer Efficiency and Error Rate of Metasurface-Based SWIPT
abstract: In this paper, an accurate and efficient analysis method of simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) based on metasurface is presented and studied. For the wireless power transfer (WPT) and wireless information transmission (WIT) parts of the SWIPT system, the proposed method can analyze the WPT transfer efficiency and WIT bit error rate of the receivers in vertical direction. To further verify the accuracy of the proposed method, a SWIPT system based on a 1-bit reconfigurable reflective metasurface operating at 5 GHz is adopted to transmit power and information through a directional beam. Measurement show that the predicted results of the proposed method are very close to the actual data, which can be used to efficiently estimate the transmission quality of SWIPT system.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: A Stream Allocation Method for MU-MIMO Communications in WLAN
abstract: In the multi-user multiple-in multiple-out (MU-MIMO) communication scenario of wireless local area network (WLAN), it is the basis for ensuring high-speed data transmission that appropriate space-time data streams are allocated to users. In this paper, a method of allocating space-time data streams for multi-user MIMO communications in WLAN is proposed, including initialization and update of streams. The initialization part is used for the initial allocation of streams for each user according to the total number of streams and users at the beginning of communication. The update part is used for determining the minimum and maximum of streams of a user when the streams of the user need to be reallocated due to changes in communication environment and process. As the number of streams changes for that user, the range of streams of other users are calculated synchronously, so as to help the network to reallocate space-time data streams. Numerical results show that the proposed method can effectively accomplish multi-user space-time data stream allocation compared to existing methods aiming at maximizing throughput, satisfying the limitation of the number of streams specified in WLAN protocols, and can support the reallocation of streams for each user in real time.

articleTitle: A Wideband Omnidirectional Vertically Polarized Patch Antenna Fed with Coplanar L-Probe
abstract: In this paper, a wideband omnidirectional vertically polarized patch antenna is proposed. This antenna is composed of seven microstrip patch antennas with the coplanar L-shaped probe. Seven horizontally polarized microstrip antennas are arranged rotationally symmetrically to form the rotationally symmetrical current distribution in the horizontal plane, which can produce a vertically polarized omnidirectional radiation pattern. The proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 28.9% (VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leqslant 2$</tex>) from 5.62 to 7.52 GHz, and has an out-of-roundness of less than 0.1 dB in the H-plane. The antenna has a good application prospect in the satellite communication of UAVs.

articleTitle: A 1-Watt X-band High Efficiency Power Amplifier in 0.15-μm GaAs p-HEMT Technology
abstract: In this paper, a low insertion loss 4-to-1 power combiner is presented for implementation of an 8–12 GHz high efficiency power amplifier (PA). Utilizing matching techniques and proper transistor sizing, the proposed three-stage common-source PA achieves a saturated output power of 30-31.4 dBm with a peak power added efficiency of 40.08 % over the operating frequency band. Besides, the simulated results show that its flat small signal gain is 23.5 ± 1 dB, the input and output return loss are below -15 dB and -9 dB, respectively. The chip is designed in 0.15-μm GaAs p-HEMT technology with a compact area of 2×2.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, including all RF and dc pads.

articleTitle: Wideband Dual Circularly Polarized Open-Ended Waveguide Antenna
abstract: A wideband dual circularly polarized antenna element based on open-ended waveguides is proposed in this paper. It adopts a cross-shaped structure with two orthogonal staggered arms, and each arm corresponds to a rectangular open-ended waveguide. Feed waveguides are respectively arranged on the side of the wide walls of the two open-ended waveguide arms, and the left-handed circularly polarization (LHCP), as well as the right-handed circularly polarization (RHCP) are excited. This structure removes the high axial ratio from the working band, thus realizing a wider axial ratio bandwidth. It is shown from the simulated results that the proposed dual circularly polarization open-ended waveguide antenna has an LHCP axial ratio band-width of 27.3 % and an RHCP axial ratio bandwidth of 28.5 %. This design lays the foundation for the subsequent construction of large-size arrays.

articleTitle: A Dual Circularly-Polarized Patch Array Antenna for Full-Duplex Communications
abstract: This work presents a solution of the dual circularly-polarized (CP) antenna with wideband inter-port isolation for full-duplex communications. It is constructed on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> patch array, and by meticulously organizing its feeding ports and network, the inter-port coupling signals may be simplified. The residual interport coupling is then eliminated using a decoupling network. Simulation results show that the presented dual-CP antenna has an inter-port isolation higher than 40 dB at the band of 5.25~5.95 GHz and peak gains of 10.2 dB for both ports.

articleTitle: Improving Front-to-Back Ratio of Base Station Antenna Array With a Modified Reflector
abstract: An antenna array with a high front-to-back ratio (FBR) permits low interference for other arrays in the backward region. In this paper, a modified reflector is designed for improving the FBR of a dual-polarized cross-dipole linear base station antenna array. The stair-shaped baffles on the edges of the reflector are used to suppress the backward diffraction field. To further improve FBR, arrow-shaped periodic units are cut on the reflector which uses the transmission field to cancel the backward radiated field. The simulated results show a 13–18 dB improvement of the FBR across the frequency band 690–960 MHz and the antenna array maintains a stable radiation performance and compact size.

articleTitle: Unambiguous Target Localization and Tracking for Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar via Cognitive Beamforming
abstract: In this paper, a cognitive transmit frequency allocation approach is proposed for unambiguous target tracking in distributed coherent aperture radar (DCAR). A crucial issue for DCAR is that the ultra-long spacing among each unit radar will generate severe grating lobes (GLs), which will deteriorate the detection performance considerably. It is shown that the locations of GLs are determined by the transmit signal frequency. In the proposed approach, the transmit signal frequency and beam steering are sequentially decided through history observations to overcome the ambiguity. Cost function is adopted as the optimization metric. Simulation results illustrates that the proposed method is able to automatically focus the beampattern toward the target direction unambiguously.

articleTitle: Design of wideband honeycomb frequency selective surface structure
abstract: In this paper, a bandpass FSS combining two-dimensional (2D) planar structure and three-dimensional (3D) structure is proposed. Each unit consists of three layers: the up-per and lower layers are identical paper-based honeycomb structures with slotlines, while the middle layer is PCB (printed circuit board) with hexagonal loops. This structure is not only light in weight, but also has good mechanical strength. Equivalent circuit method is used to assist the analysis, and S-parameters from both full-wave simulation and circuit simulation are presented and compared. The simulation results show that the FSS can generate a wide passband from 3.38 GHz to 8.95 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Antenna Based on Aperture-Coupled Magneto-Electric Dipole for Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a wideband magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is designed, fabricated, and measured. The coaxial probe and aperture coupling technique are employed to excite the ME-dipole. The measured results show that the proposed antenna has the -10dB impedance bandwidth from 18 to 29.5 GHz leading to a 48.1% fractional bandwidth, and a stable gain over the whole operating bandwidth. The antenna element has a compact size of 0.58 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}\times 0.45\lambda_{0}\times 0.17\lambda_{0}$</tex>. With the advantages of wide bandwidth, stable gain and miniaturization, the proposed antenna has great application potential in millimeter wave communication system.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Triple-Band Directionl Coupler Based on Integrated Passive Devices Process
abstract: In this paper, a 3dB directional coupler with high performance using Integrated Passive Devices (IPD) process is designed. To achieve strong coupling, floating ground-plane conductor (FGPC) is etched on the ground plane. In addition, the wiggly-coupled lines are adopted to improve directivity. The result shows that the proposed IPD coupler has good performance in three bands, which potentially provides a innovative idea for designing harmonic-controlled Radio Frequency Power Amplifier (RFPA) circuits based on heterogeneous integration (HI).

articleTitle: A Discontinuous Galerkin Multiregion Integral Equation for Multiscale Antenna Analysis
abstract: Aiming at the efficient radiation simulation of anten-nas with dielectric slabs and spatial multiscale features, a discon-tinuous Galerkin (DG) scheme for the multi-region surface inte-gral equation is presented in this letter. Boundary lines between different materials can be handled independently without merging and reducing unknowns at the junction, which simplifies the cal-culation. Numerical experiments of different kinds of antennas are carried out to verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method through comparisons.

articleTitle: A High Radiation Efficiency and Low-cost Comb Antenna Array Based on SISL for 24 GHz Band Application
abstract: In this paper, a high radiation efficiency and low-cost comb antenna array based on substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) is proposed for 24 GHz automotive radar. The antenna consists of five layers of dielectric substrates and 10 metal layers. By introducing an open stub between the feed line and the antenna, the antenna impedance bandwidth is increased (22.25-24.58) GHz. With a gain of 14.6 dBi at 24 GHz and a beamwidth of 53° and 13° for E-plane and H-plane, the antenna is able to achieve higher gain with fewer units compared to the same type of comb antenna and is constructed using a lower cost FR4 dielectric substrate.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Space-frequency Beamforming using Time Delay Lines
abstract: The space-frequency beamforming is one of the most popular and effective structures for ultra wideband beamforming (UWB). In this paper, subband beamforming using tapped delay lines (TDLs), namely, TDLs-SB, is proposed for obtaining a satisfactory performance on ultra wideband passband. The TDL is originally used for space-time beamforming, however, the TDLSB is innovatively used TDLs for space-frequency beamforming with more degrees of freedom, resulting in perfect sidelobe characteristic and accurate beam pointing for ultra wideband signal. Simulations highlight the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed structure and algorithms for 1 GHz wideband passband, and the novel structure can process more than 1 GHz passband for beamforming.

articleTitle: In-Line Microstrip Filters with Ease-of-Control Transmission Zeros Based on Frequency-Variant Parallel Coupled Structures
abstract: This paper presents a reasonable solution, based on a direct synthesis approach, for high selectivity microstrip filters by using frequency variant parallel-coupled structures. The approach relies on the analysis and modelling of two elementary structures gathering parallel-coupled microstrips with grounded or open stubs. Note that the resultant circuit models require only a few circuit parameters and are found equivalent to a pair of resonators & a frequency-variant coupling (FVC) in between. The FVC produces a transmission zero (TZ) natively, whose position can be easily assigned (either above or below the passband) and controlled depending on the shunt stub situation. In consequence, high selectivity microstrip filters with multiple TZs can thus be realized by properly arrowing the proposed structures. For the validation, we carry out an illustrative example along with simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: A 24-29.5 GHz Compact Receiver Front End with Differential Image Rejection Filter in 65nm CMOS for 5G Application
abstract: A 24-29.5 GHz compact receiver front end in 65nm CMOS for 5G millimeter-wave application is presented in this paper. A compact differential image rejection filter structure is used to achieve effective image suppression and good impedance matching between LNA and mixer. The image rejection of the filter is realized by an out-of-band zero point generated by the double ring rectangular resonator. Designed and implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology with 1-V supply, the proposed receiver front end realizes that the conversion gain of 25 dB to 33.4 dB and the image signal suppression of 33.5 dB to 60.5 dB from 24 GHz to 29.5 GHz. The chip size is only 0.49 mm2 excluding all DC PADs.

articleTitle: Dual-Circularly-Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
abstract: Dual-circularly-polarized magneto-electric(ME) dipole for satellite system is proposed in the paper. The results indicate the design has the excellent results. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 10.7-14.9GHz, and the antenna's axial ratio bandwidth is about 32.8%. The results indicate that both polars have similar performance. The antenna has a size of 10.3mm*10.3mm*3.4mm, which is suitable for implementations in phased array. In order to improve performance of the antenna, the wide-angle impedance matching(WAIM) layer is used. Air hole is punched all around the WAIM in order to improve isolation between elements in the array.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Mechanically Beam-Scanning Antenna System
abstract: We propose a mechanically-controlled, onedimensional wide-angle beam-scanning antenna operating in the ka-band frequency range. Our antenna design is based on the folded transmitarray concept and offers a low-profile, high-gain solution for wide-angle beam-scanning applications. To improve the antenna's performance, we use the bifocal technique to compensate for phase variations, reducing gain loss within the scanning range. We simulated the antenna's performance using Ansys HFSS, which showed that it can scan within a range of ±28°, with a peak gain of 22.7 dBi and a maximum gain loss of 1.4 dB.

articleTitle: A Miniature D-Band GaAs Low-Noise Amplifier with Customized On-Chip Terahertz Devices
abstract: This paper presents design and verification of a miniature D-band GaAs low noise amplifier (LNA) in 70 nm mHEMT GaA <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> technology. Symmetry cap partition and serpentine CPW configuration are proposed to extend self-resonating frequency and reduce area respectively. By these solution and technique, the designed GaAs low noise amplifier has obtained more than 7.3 dB small signal gain at 135–154 GHz with 11.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}$</tex> peak gain at 152 GHz. Its measured noise figure is less than 8.8 dB at the range of 136GHz to 154 GHz. The overall chip area including sealing ring is only 0.88 mm2.

articleTitle: A 100MS/s 12 Bit SAR-assisted Pipeline ADC with Gain-enhanced Fully Differential Ring Amplifier
abstract: A 12 bit 100 MS/s SAR-assisted pipeline ADC with a 6-bit SAR ADC for the first stage and a 7-bit SAR ADC for the second stage is presented. The sub-ADCs adopt the upper plate sampling asynchronous SAR logic. The gain-enhanced fully differential ring amplifier acts as a residue amplifier, providing high-precision settling and accommodating large signal swings. The cascoded output stages are designed in the ring amplifier to enhance the closed loop accuracy.
