A prototype ADC has been designed and simulated using TSMC65nm CMOS technology, and it operates with a standard 1.2 V supply voltage.The SNDR and ENOB is 63.6dB and 10.28bit respectively from the simulation results, with a Nyquist frequency input sampled at 100 MS/s. The ADC achieves a FoM of 32.01 fJ/conversion-step.

articleTitle: A 110-160GHz Wideband Power Amplifier in 0.13μm SiGe BiCMOS with 14.12dBm Psat and 9.26% PAE
abstract: This paper presents a single-ended wideband power amplifier (PA) in 130nm SiGe process, which achieves a wide operating frequency range, while also exhibiting considerable saturated output power and efficiency. In order to extended bandwidth, low-Q impedance matching networks are adopted. Cascode topology and gain-boosting technology are also employed to improve the efficiency and saturated output power, respectively. Verified by the EM simulation of passive components and post-simulation, the PA operates from 110GHz to 163GHz (3dB bandwidth) with a peak gain of 24dB at 140GHz. Consuming DC power of 0.26W from 2.8-V supply voltage, the PA achieves peak output power of 14.12 dBm at 150GHz and competitive power-added-efficiency (PAE) of 9.2% over the bandwidth from 144GHz to 156GHz. The chip occupies an area of 0.26 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding the pads.

articleTitle: A 60GHz 6-bit Digital-Step Attenuator with Low Phase Variations and Amplitude in 40-nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper designs a 6-bit digital attenuator that operates at 60GHz millimeter wave based on the TSMC 40nm CMOS process. The attenuation range is 0-31.5dB with a step of 0.5dB. The attenuator is composed of cascaded bridge- T,pi and improved- T structures, and an inductive compensation struc-ture is added to reduce additional phase shift. Interstage matching is designed to reduce the load effect between stages. By rea-sonably selecting the parameter model and topology, optimizing the layout design, the circuit performance is achieved and the simulation results are as follows: Within the range of 26-64GHz, RMS attenuation error <0.5dB, RMS additional phase shift <2.7°, insertion loss at 60GHz is 6.75dB, attenuation error is 0.15dB, 1dB gain compression point is 11.54dBm.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Wideband On-Chip Antenna Based on Characteristic Modes Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a terahertz wideband on-chip antenna in TSMC 65nm process. The characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is used to guide the antenna design, and the wideband performance of the antenna is achieved by selecting the appropriate characteristic modes. A metal plane is added under the antenna substrate to reflect the electromagnetic wave leaked to the substrate and improve the antenna efficiency. The overall area of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$800\text{um}\times 800\text{um}$</tex>. The simulation results show that the antenna achieves the maximum gain of 7.6dBi at 300GHz, a 110GHz 3dB bandwidth (BW) from 280GHz–383GHz, and a 73GHz–10dB impedance bandwidth from 260GHz- 325GHz. The maximum radiation efficiency is 45% at 306GHz.

articleTitle: A Tunable Microstrip Low-Pass Filter Using Defected Ground Structures
abstract: A tunable microstrip low-pass filter (LPF) using defected ground structure (DGS) is presented in this paper. The presented filter consists of five tunable DGS units and microstrip transmission lines on the top layer. In order to tune the cut-off frequency of the LPF, varactor diodes are loaded at the middle of the DGS on the bottom layer. Compared with the conventional dumbbell-shaped DGS, an isolated patch is added to facilitate the addition of bias circuit of varactor diode. The isolated patch is coupled with ground layer by interdigital structure, which is helpful to extend the tuning range of the tunable DGS unit. The tuning mechanism of proposed tunable LPF is simple, the five varactor diodes can be controlled by a single reverse bias voltage, and no DC-block capacitors is utilized in the tunable filter. The filter is optimized with HFSS, simulation results show that RL (return loss) is greater than 12dB during the passband, and the 3 dB cut-off frequency can be tuned from 4.57 GHz to 6.29 GHz by varying the reverse bias voltage Vdc from 30V to 0V, besides, the stopband of the filter can be expanded to 10 GHz with a rejection level of 20 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Millimeter-Wave Broadband Transceiver for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: Broadband wireless communication for unmanned aerial vehicle could be improved with millimeter-wave technology. In this study, we present a demonstration system for millimeter-wave broadband wireless communication. The technology employs frequency domain equalization along with single-carrier transmission (SC-FDE). The aerial communication channel is fitted with a special frame structure. A feed-forward synchronization technique is offered at the receiver side to speed up signal capture, and an iterative frequency domain equalizer is simplified for high-speed implementation. An experiment using a two-path frequency selective channel that achieves a data rate of 1Gbps with a 16QAM signal serves as a demonstration of the system performance.

articleTitle: Filtering Balun Design using Hairpin-Ring Resonator and SSPP Metamaterial with Wide Notched band and Wide Stopband
abstract: In this paper, a novel filtering balun based on microstrip-to-slotline transition is proposed. Utilizing the inherent out-of-phase electric field distributions on the adjacent grounds of slotline, the balun function is realized. In order to realize the wide notched-band and stopband performance for radio astronomical applications, spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) metamaterial and multi-mode hairpin ring resonators (HRRs) are adopted. With these novel structures loaded, the proposed filtering balun exhibits a wide band from 1GHz to 6 GHz. The notched band is from 3.2 GHz to 4.4 GHz, within the notched band, the rejection level is better than 15 dB. Besides, the out-of-band suppression is below 35 dB in the wide frequency range from 6 GHz to 8 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Low RCS Hybrid Metasurface Array Antenna with Circularly Polarization
abstract: This letter presents a hybrid metasurface antenna with wideband low radar cross-section (RCS) characteristic radiating circularly-polarized (CP) electromagnetic (EM) waves. To further expand the frequency band of RCS reduction, the high frequency resistive layer is introduced into the antenna element. The numerical simulation shows that the inserted layer has no effect on the radiation performance of the antenna array. Then, the proposed element and its orthogonal unit are arranged in checkerboard pattern, and the metasurface array antenna has a maximum gain of 16.7dBi. The mechanism of RCS reduction depended on absorption and phase cancellation. Compared with the reference array, the proposed metasurface antenna can reduce the RCS at 6 to 20 GHz.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Hollow Rectangular Dielectric Waveguide
abstract: A low-loss hollow rectangular dielectric waveguide (HRDW) is proposed and investigated for sub-terahertz (sub- THz) applications. It is a longitudinally homogeneous three-layer structure constructed by the same material, with a hollow core in the middle. It supports monomode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{11}^{y}$</tex> over 220–280 GHz. Hollow structure can significantly reduce the material absorption loss. The proposed waveguide is designed under PCB technology. The simulated results show that the average attenuation constant of the HRDW is 0.017 dB/mm in the designated band, which is reduced by 55% compared with the narrowed dielectric microstrip line (N-DML). The proposed dielectric waveguide can be used for sub-THz application due to the advantage of low loss, simple structure and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: Single-Satellite Interference Geolocation using Rainfall Data
abstract: Passive geolocation of an interference emitter using a single geostationary satellite is considered. The proposed geolocation approach exploits the attenuation effect of rainfall on the received satellite signal, only measures the power fluctuation of the interfering signal over a period of time, then performs similarity analysis on the signal attenuation and the rainfall characteristics of different regions to determine the emitter's location. We introduce the concept of time series analysis to geolocation and propose the application of dynamic time warping in geolocation. Experiments with real-world data verify the feasibility of this geolocation approach.

articleTitle: A LTCC - Based Flat Dual - Polarized Long - Slot Array Antenna for Millimeter - Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter wave dual-polarized planar array antenna based on low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC), with high integration and simple feed network is proposed. Dielectric parallel plate waveguide (PPW) is used to feed vertically inserted long-slot radiation elements, to realize dual polarized radiation with high isolation. Two 1:8 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) power dividers are arranged orthogonally to provide line sources for the PPW. The simulation and test results show that the reflection coefficient of the antenna is less than -10 dB in the 29–32 GHz frequency band, and the port isolation is greater than 30 dB. In the 30–32 GHz frequency band, the antenna gain is about 19 dBi, and the cross polarization level is lower than -25 dB. Compared with multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) process, LTCC enables higher design accuracy and better packaging characteristics, and can be applied to highly integrated millimeter wave microsystem.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Modeling and Optimization of Multi-State Filters
abstract: The multi-state tunble filter in microwave area is widely used in many aspects. Actually we hope there can be a geometrically determined filter which possesses different frequency characteristics. And we can change its filter states by conveniently altering some specific parameters. To precisely and efficiently achieve the design of this kind of tunable filter, this paper review a unique technique with the help of ANN optimization and multiple novel algorithms. Considering the particularity of the filter, we use two sets of parameters as input during modeling. Parameters related to geometric dimensions are non-tunable parameters, and parameters related to filter state turning are tunable parameters. After optimization, we can obtain the value of the parameters under the desired response. The whole model consists of multiple sub-models and corresponds to the tuning states. All sub-models share non-tunable parameters and each sub-model has its corresponding tunable parameters. In order to ensure the accuracy of the optimization, both tunable and non-tunable parameters will be obtained simultaneously and constrained by all tuning states. Moreover, a trust-region algorithm is used to improve the convergence in the process of multiple tuning states optimization.

articleTitle: An Out-of-Band Low RCS Microstrip Patch Antenna Using a Back-Loaded Triplexer
abstract: An out-of-band low RCS microstrip patch antenna using a back-loaded triplexer is proposed in this paper. By designing the working frequency band of the triplexer within that of the antenna, the frequency band of the antenna can be divided into three bands. Taking band 2 of the triplexer as the actual working band of the low RCS antenna, and designing the matching load for bands 1 and 3, the incident waves in the out-of-band of the low RCS antenna can be absorbed, and the out-of-band low RCS performance can be realized. The simulated result shows that the RCS of the proposed antenna is reduced by 20 dB at 7.25 GHz and 23 dB at 8.7 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A Four-Way High-Power Combiner Employing Hybrid Microstrip and Waveguide Structure
abstract: This paper presents an X-band four-way high-power combiner employing hybrid microstrip and waveguide structure. To satisfy the requirement of compact configuration and high power capacity, the power combiner adopts a four-way hybrid microstrip and waveguide architecture. The input network adopts the microstrip prototype and the output network utilizes waveguide structure. To verify the design concept, the proposed configuration is designed, fabricated, and measured. The experimental outcomes indicate that the proposed power combiner achieves a bandwidth of 9.2 to 10.8 GHz with a minimum insertion loss of 1.52 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Structurally Embedded High-Temperature Resistant Antenna with High Isolation and Wide Beam
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band structurally embedded high-temperature resistant antenna operating at X-band and Ka-band is designed with high isolation and wide beam. The dual-band antenna is composed of a ceramic dielectric double-sided printed dipole antenna (DSPDA) connected with substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and a ceramic dielectric rod antenna (DRA) fed by the dielectric-filled waveguide, whose broadside is replaced by the SIW. High isolation performance can be realized due to polarization orthogonality between DSPDA and DRA. The dual-band antenna is embedded in the center position of the thermal insulation material, which is packaged by the thermal protection shield. Because of the lower thermal conductivity of the ceramic dielectric of DRA and the longer gap between DSPDA and the top of the thermal protection shield, the high-temperature resistant antenna can achieve good thermal insulation performance. Under the continuous time of the 1900s and surface heat source temperature of 1200°C, the feed ports can be kept within 165°C

articleTitle: A Robust Deterministic Neighbor Discovery in Ad Hoc Networks with Directional Antennas
abstract: In this article, a robust neighbor discovery algorithm on the foundation of the deterministic algorithm is proposed to face the collision case, which is a common phenomenon when more than one neighbor exists in one directional beam. Furthermore, the random transceiver is taken into account in the deterministic algorithm, and a theoretical analysis of the algorithm is given. The relationship between the upper-bound of the average neighbor discovery time and node density for both 1-way and 2-way handshake mechanisms is then theoretically derived. Finally, the effectiveness of our approach is shown through simulations.

articleTitle: Image-to-Image Translation-Based Millimeter-Wave Beam Search Using Out-of-Band Spatial Information
abstract: The large-scale antenna array brings great gains to the millimeter wave (mmWave) communication system, but the consequent beam search overhead is evident. A feasible solution is to exploit the spatial congruence between signals in different frequency bands and use spatial information to help establish a mmWave link. Using out-of-band information, an image-to-image translation-based beam search method is proposed. Paired power azimuth spectrum images are used to train the model, and the mmWave angle information is predicted using spatial information of the sub-6 GHz band. Prediction results can help the mmWave communication system largely compress the beam search range. Simulation results verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis on the influence of two-layer rough interface on the echo characteristics of buried rectangular target in composite electromagnetic scattering
abstract: In order to analyze the influence of scattering from two layer underground rough surfaces on the echo of buried target, a finite-difference time-domain calculation model for ground penetrating radar detection of two media rough surfaces and a rectangular target is established. The composite scattering echoes of two rough interfaces with a rectangular target at different root mean square heights and different correlation lengths are calculated respectively. The influence of two-layer rough surface scattering on target echo is discussed and analyzed, as well as the effect of roughness parameter root mean square height and correlation length on target echo shape.

Author Keywords: two-layer rough interface GPR echo characteristics

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave and Sub-THz Wireless the Wire Towards 6G
abstract: The Lead6G project targets a monolithic, highly integrated THz chipset, which includes the active channels and the antennas on one piece of silicon to overcome the challenges for the THz chipset: power, packaging, size. The multi-channel interpolation-based beamforming could improve the radiated power and receiver sensitivity while decreasing its power consumption. The on-chip dual-polarized antenna array would simplify the packaging at THz frequency and increase its bandwidth. The low-loss on-chip metamaterial structure would tightly confine electromagnetic waves and optimize chipset radiation.

articleTitle: Encoding Network Optimization with Phase Quantization for the Machine-Learning-based Coding Digital Receiving Array
abstract: Recently, a novel machine-learning-based coding digital receiving array (ML-CDRA) has been proposed: the received array signals are encoded into few radio frequency (RF) channels, and decoded by an artificial neural network in real-time. However, compared to the traditional full-channel digital receiving array (DRA), the maximum signal noise ratio (SNR) after digital beam-forming (DBF) is reduced in different directions. This paper proposes an encoding network optimization algorithm for ML-CDRA based on gradient descent to improve the maximum SNR after DBF in the desired directions. The phase quantization of the encoding network is also introduced in the proposed algorithm. Simulation results show that the ML-CDRA with the optimized encoding network can significantly improve the maximum SNR after DBF in the desired directions.

articleTitle: A Wireless Power Transfer Design for Omnidirectional Joint
abstract: In this paper, a wireless power transfer (WPT) structure using only a pair of coupling coils is proposed for application at omnidirectional joint. Firstly, based on the theoretical analysis of the stability of the WPT at the joint, all the variables affecting the stable transmission are obtained. Secondly, the trajectory equation of the receiving (Rx) coil relative to the transmitting (Tx) coil during the rotation is determined by the coordinate system transformation theory, and then the mutual inductance of Rx and Tx coils at different pinch angles is obtained. Finally, the optimal values of the above variables, i.e., the final WPT structure, are obtained by minimizing the mutual inductance fluctuation deviation in the available range of 60-180°. By using the proposed transmission structure, a coupler operating is designed and the results show an efficiency fluctuation deviation of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm6.5\%$</tex> in the 120° operating range.

articleTitle: A U-Band Low-Noise Amplifier MMIC in 100-nm GaN Process
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a 100-nm GaN low-voltage low noise amplifier (LNA) MMIC operating in the frequency range of 40 to 65 GHz. The suggested LNA achieves a gain flatness of less than 1.5 dB and a small signal gain of 20.5 dB throughout the whole bandwidth. The Sl1 and S22 both fall below -10 dB. Between 50 and 65 GHz, the noise figure (NF) approaches an average value of 2.7 dB. Moreover, a 5 V supply can provide 350mW dc power consumption with an average I-dB compression point output power (OP1dB) of greater than 15 dBm in U-band. As a result, it may not only be crucial for the front-end link of the communication transceiver but also as the driver of the transmitter's power amplifier.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Filtering Patch Antenna Using Fan-Shaped Strips and Slots Structures
abstract: A novel filtering patch antenna that offers high gain and wide bandwidth performance is presented in this letter. The antenna features a square patch with a pair of Fan-shaped strips and two slots. By embedding two symmetrical Fan-shaped strips, which in turn generates an additional resonance mode and a lower-band null on the left side of the passband. By cutting two slots along the radiating edges of the patch, a radiation null can be achieved on the right side of the passband. A rectangular strip is etched below the substrate and connected with the feeding probe, which can improve the impedance match and increase the level of out-of-band suppression on the right side of the passband. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert < -10$</tex> dB) is 13.9% (2.28-2.61 GHz). With a maximum gain of 9.77 dBi in the passband, the presented antenna achieves two radiation nulls at 2.20 GHz and 2.73 GHz, respectively. Furthermore, the out-of-band suppression level on both sides of the passband exceeds 15.8 dB.

articleTitle: 7 mm Band Cryogenic Receiver of NanShan 26m Radio Telescope
abstract: In combination with the needs of VLBI joint measurement and molecular spectral line and other radio astronomy observation, the Microwave Technology Laboratory of the Xinjiang Astronomical Observatory has developed a 7mm band cryogenic receiver for the NanShan 26-meter Radio Telescope. The receiver has a working frequency of 30-50GHz, a dual-beam design, and uses the feed integrated cooling technology. The dual-circular polarization signal output by the ortho-mode transducer is converted into 70-1024MHz IF signal by the down-conversion unit and output. After the installation and commissioning of the NSRT, the noise temperature of the test receiver meets the design index. Recently, the 7mm band receiver participated in the 43GHz joint test of European VLBI Network for the first time and successfully obtained interference fringes. In the next step, it is planned to use the 7mm band receiver to carry out single-antenna scientific observation such as molecular spectral lines.

articleTitle: A High Selectivity Filtering Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Stub-Loading
abstract: A stub-loaded filtering dielectric resonator (DR) antenna with high roll-off selectivity is proposed 5G N78 application. A rectangular DR is applied to serve as the radiator. A rec-tangular slot is etched on the center of the ground plane to realize coupled feeding. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{111}$</tex> mode of the DR radiator is successful-ly excited. Then, a quarter-wavelength short-circuited stub is added to the coupled feeding line, which can introduce a radiation null below the passband. Similarly, a quarter-wavelength open-circuited stub is connected to the coupled slot. As a result, a radiation null above the operational band is introduced. Here, a good filtering gain response is realized. To further verify the performance, the proposed filtering DR antenna is fabricated and measured. It has a small size of 0.27 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0} \times 0.27\lambda_{0}\times 0.126\lambda_{0}$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free space wavelength at 3.6 GHz), a bandwidth of 20.0%, a realized gain of 6.04 dBi, a total efficiency of -0.46 dB (89.81%) and a filtering response with lower / upper selectivity of 130.3 dB/GHz / 139.6 dB/GHz.

articleTitle: High Performance Dual-Band Filter With Flexible Frequency Allocation Using Hybrid Boundary Dual-Mode Dielectric Resonator
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band filter with flexible frequency allocation is proposed using novel dual-mode T-shaped dielectric resonator (DR). Benefiting from the hybrid electromagnetic boundary and triangular chamfers on DRs, dual-mode frequencies could be manipulated independently while keeping wide spurious-free window. Then not only tiny but also large frequency ratios could be both achieved via the presented structure. Moreover, mechanisms of independent adjustments on external and internal couplings are investigated, facilitating flexible dual-band bandwidth control. For verification, a three-order dual-band filter operating at 1.8 and 2.1 GHz is designed. The exhibited low loss and high selectivity within compact size illustrate the proposed filter at high-standard multiband communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band/Wideband Dipole MIMO Antennas Using Center-Loaded Stubs
abstract: In this paper, a design method for dual-band and wideband MIMO antennas is presented. Two stubs are loaded at the center point of a dipole antenna so that two hybrid modes can be generated. For the dual-band design, the fundamental mode works at a lower frequency while the second harmonic mode works at a higher frequency. For the wideband design, the original main stub of the dipole antenna works at a lower frequency, and half of the main dipole together with the loaded stubs works at a higher frequency. The dual-band antenna's optimal frequency range is 3.4 - 3.6 GHz and 4.7 - 5 GHz, and its isolation is greater than 18 dB with an ECC of less than 0.025. The final optimized wideband MIMO antenna achieves isolation of better than 15dB across the desired N78 band, from 3.3 to 3.8 GHz, with an ECC of less than 0.17.

articleTitle: PIN Diodes Loaded 1-Bit Cylindrical Conformal Reconfigurable Transmitarray Antenna
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit cylindrical conformal recon-figurable transmitarray antenna (CRTA) is proposed, and an element that adopts the structure of active and parasitic bypass dipole receiving and passive slotted rectangular patch transmit-ting is presented. Compared to the transmitarray elements that have already been proposed, the element has a much thinner substrate, with a thickness of only 1. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$08\text{mm}(0.054 \lambda_{0})$</tex>. The con-formal transmitarray consists of 12 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 12$</tex> elements and can achieve beam scanning within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 50^{\circ}$</tex> angle range. Furthermore, the transmitarray has an overall gain of 19.7dB and has 5% of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\text{dB}$</tex> relative bandwidth. The presented CRT A can provide a reference for the application of the RTA on non-flat carrier plat-forms in the future.

articleTitle: Neuro-Tf Modeling of Fourth-order Waveguide Filter Using Padé via Lanczos and EM Sensitivities
abstract: The neuro-transfer function (neuro-TF) modeling method has a wide range of applications in the field of electromagnetic (EM) parametric modeling. Matrix Padé via Lanczos (MPVL) technique is executed repeatedly to generate training data. To solve the issue of poles-mismatch, a novel pole-/zero-matching algorithm using EM sensitivities has been proposed. The feasibility of the neuro-TF modeling method is proved by an example of a fourth-order waveguide filter.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging of Human Body from Point Cloud with Capsule Network
abstract: 3D microwave imaging of human targets has potential applications in military detection and intelligent interaction fields, we propose an auto-encoder-like capsule network to complete this task. We make two different 3D microwave imaging datasets MI-1 and MI-2 for verifying this work, the human action in MI-1 changes greatly, and the human action in MI-2 changes slightly. Experimental results show that our capsule network achieves nice results on both MI-1 and MI-2 datasets.

articleTitle: Excitation of Circular Waveguide $\text{TE}_{01}$ Mode of Microwave Communication for Downhole While Drilling
abstract: In this paper, circular waveguide TE01 mode is ex-ploited to improve the distance of the single-stage signal trans-mission of microwave communication for downhole while drilling (MCDWD) technology in gas drilling for 5-inch API drill pipe. The excitation of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode which is suitable in the downhole for gas drilling with high velocity gas flow is proposed. Firstly, a rectangular waveguide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{10}$</tex> modes is excited by the probe, and then the rectangular waveguide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{20}$</tex> mode is generated using the TE20 mode converter with a longitudinal E-plane metal plate which enhances the purity of the TE20 mode. Subsequently, the waveguide height is increased through the stepped waveguide which reduces the effect of the higher order modes. Finally, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{20}$</tex> mode is converted into circular waveguide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{01}$</tex> mode through the gradual structure. The simulation shows that the return loss of the proposed structure is less than -15 dB in the frequency range from 6.25 GHz to 6.45 GHz, and the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode conversion rate is higher than 93.6%.

Author Keywords: microwave communication for downhole while drilling

articleTitle: Three Compact Active Baluns with High Phase/Amplitude Balance and Low Power in 65-nm CMOS for Transceiver Applications
abstract: Three types of 400M-1000MHz compact active baluns with high phase/amplitude balance and low power for transceiver applications are presented in this paper. Three architectures are single transistor balun, common-gate/common-source(CG-CS) balun and active current mirror balun. These baluns were fabricated by 65-nm CMOS technology. The measurement shows phase imbalance and amplitude imbalance are 180.78° /0.19dB, 178.3° /0.12dB and 178.7° /1.42dB at 650MHz, respectively. The power consumption is 4.56mW, 22.5mW and 13.67mW under 1-V power supply. Three baluns occupy 0.0256mm2, 0.024mm2 and 0.0184mm2 excluding pads.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metamaterial Devices Based on New Materials for Wireless Communication Fields
abstract: With the development of wireless communication, aerospace, and other emerging technologies, the spectral resources within the 0.1~10 THz range have attracted widespread attention and research from numerous scholars. Terahertz devices based on graphene and vanadium dioxide possess strong application potential in the terahertz field due to their advantages in novel materials, low frequency bands, ultra-broad bandwidth, multi-band, miniaturization, and multifunctionality. However, current terahertz devices have complex structures, large volumes, narrow working bandwidths, higher frequency bands, and difficulties in processing and testing. Moreover, most devices employ traditional materials, hindering the commercialization of terahertz technology in various markets and applications. In this presentation, we will address these challenges and outline the research progress in this field, and introducing our recent work. Including graphene and vanadium dioxide broadband-narrowband terahertz absorbers, vanadium dioxide ultra-broadband terahertz absorbers, and graphene low-frequency absorbers. Finally, we will discuss the development prospects and trends of terahertz devices.

articleTitle: A High-efficiency 135 – 155 GHz Power Amplifier with Compact Three-Conductor Power Combiner Balun in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: A compact power amplifier (PA) design for D-band applications in 130nm SiGe BiCMOS technology with saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) excess of 13dBm covering 20GHz operation bandwidth is presented. This architecture consisted of a three-stage driver and one-stage power differential configuration, and the compact three-conductor balun is embedded to improve the output power level. The design delivers 13dBm with 40dB gain from 135 - 155GHz, and the maximum P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> is 13.9dBm with a peak power-added-efficiency (PAE) of 24% at 145GHz. The proposed three-conductor balun achieves a good performance of transmission loss that is less than 1dB in the range of 130 - 170GHz, and the amplitude/phase imbalance is not more than 1dB / 3° covering 3-dB bandwidth, respectively. The 0.29W PA is capable of providing a good figure of merit (FoM) of 110 while occupying the core active area of 0.49 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Harmonic Elimination Method of RF-PWM Based on Phase-Shift Control and MPWM for All-Digital Transmitters
abstract: In this paper, a novel radio frequency pulse width modulation (RF -PWM) based on phase-shift control and mapping pulse width modulation (MPWM) is proposed. This method decomposes the modulated signal into two phase-modulated constant envelope signals by means of phase-shift control. The phase-modulated signals are directly converted to 3-level pulse waveforms after MPWM, and then a 5-level digital RF modulation signal will be fast generated through vector synthesis. In addition, the pulse width of the 5-level signal is controlled to eliminate specific subharmonic components, which can significantly reduce the design requirements of the filter. Compared with other PWM methods, it not only greatly reduces the size of the look-up table (L UT), but also improves the real-time and flexibility of all-digital transmitters (ADTx). Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of this method are verified by the simulation.

articleTitle: Quad-band Crown-Shaped Hairpin Antenna with AMC for WBAN and 5G Applications
abstract: An irregular, quad-band crown-shaped hairpin antenna with AMC-back is presented. The antenna consists of a crown-shaped radiation patch with a U-shaped slot and a defected ground structure (DGS). This configuration, with resonant frequencies at 1.44, 2.23, 3.98, and 4.49 GHz, will apply to the new generation of 5G/6G mainstream commercial bands (N77 and N79). By placing an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) with three zero-phase bands in the reflection spectra, the gain at 4 frequency points increases by 1.2, 5.21, 5.4, and 6 dBi, respectively. The directional radiation pattern obtained from the developed antenna ensures low backward radiation to the body tissue. We also got the head data using the Fourth Cole-Cole Model and established a model to calculate the specific absorption rate (SAR) value. The SAR value obtained follows the secure limit. Finally, the antenna was fabricated, and the experimental results validated the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Algorithm for Time Error Estimation in Distributed Radars
abstract: Parameter estimation, target detection and tracking capabilities of a radar system can be significantly enhanced by deploying a distributed network. In this paper, a design of partially correlated waveform is proposed as an alternative to the traditional method to make the error estimation uncomplicated, and the novel algorithm is used for estimating the time differences of transmit coherence parameters. Furthermore, the estimation algorithm for distributed dual radar systems is presented, and the coherent rendered signals are fused and separated at transmitter and receiver parts, respectively. The simulation experiments prove effectiveness and low-complexity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: COVID-SENSE: Radar-Based Remote Respiratory Disorder Detection in Clinical Environment
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic urgently requires contact-less medical monitoring to prevent human-to-human interactions. Respiratory rate and respiratory irregularity are important indicators to classify the stages of COVID-19. Thus, respiration measurement is essential for the doctors to decide on medical treatment during hospitalization. In this work, the radar-based internet of things (IoT) system was implemented in inpatient ward, and the respiratory disorder assessment algorithm was proposed to help to identify the different COVID-19 stages. Data of COVID-19 patients in different symptoms' stages were collected continuously for one week. The experimental results show the proposed system can accurately detect the real-time respiratory irregularity in a remote and convenient way. The results of detection are also consistent with the diagnosis of clinicians, which indicates the proposed system can provide a safe and reliable way for the daily health monitoring of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

articleTitle: Transient Electrothermal Analysis for System-in-Package with Unconditionally Stable Finite Difference Method
abstract: Electrothermal phenomenon in system-in-package is one of the key factors affecting its reliability. Transient analysis help describe the electrical performances over temperature and time to assess the effectiveness of the current design. In this study, we solve Maxwell's equation with the Debye model to characterize the electromagnetic field and its bidirectional coupling with the thermal field by Ohmic loss, dielectric loss, and temperature-dependent material parameters. The alternating direction implicit scheme is employed to avoid the stability condition of the finite difference method, and a time factor is used to balance the time difference between the two fields, thus improving the algorithm's efficiency significantly. The simulation ability of complex models, especially for the electrical interconnection structures of system-in-package, is realized with our transient simulation algorithm.

articleTitle: A CPW-Fed Broadband Circularly Polarized Monopole Antenna with Parasitic Open Loop
abstract: A simple and compact broadband circularly polarized (CP) monopole antenna with coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of a knife-shaped monopole, a circular-ring with a gap at the bottom, and an asymmetric ground plane. CP radiation might be produced by combining an asymmetric ground plane with a monopole. Then, a parasitic open loop is added to achieve broad CP characteristics and a wide impedance bandwidth. The simulated antenna provides -10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 113.1% ranging from 2.19 to 7.89 GHz, and the 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 77.4% ranging from 2.65-6 GHz. In addition, it provides 72.7% of 2-dB AR bandwidth in the range of 2.75 to 5.89 GHz. The performances with different parameters are analyzed. The proposed antenna can be applied to a variety of wireless communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Dynamic Adjustment of Output Back-off Range of Doherty Power Amplifier by Injection-Control
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Doherty power amplifier (DPA) architecture to dynamically adjust the output back-off (OBO) for dynamic peaking-to-average power ratio (PAPR) application. It is achieved by integrating the complex combining load with injection-control technique to adapt the high-efficiency range with OBO. The experimental results have verified that the proposed architecture can adjust the OBO from 3 dB to 7 dB at 2.4 GHz, and maintain high power-added efficiency (PAE) when the PAPR changes.

articleTitle: A Design of S to C band 45° Linear-Polarized Banyan Tree Antenna Array
abstract: The stable spatial polarization characteristic (SPC) of wide-band, wide-scanning angle phased antenna array has always been a significant challenge. A 45° linear-polarized Banyan Tree Antenna (BTA) array operated over S to C band is designed in this paper, which covers triple frequency with a maximum scanning of ±45°. The antenna element within an infinite array is designed for VSWR < 2.6 when scanning up to ±45°. Compared to traditional BTA array, we found that the matching structure at feeding position can enhance the active reflection coefficients in the operating bandwidth. An 8×8 designed antenna array was fabricated and measured for verification. The results indicate the BTA array is very good choice for use in wide-band, wide-scanning angle with 45°-linear polarized array.

articleTitle: Efficient Algorithm for Antenna Mutual Coupling on Dihedral-Corner Platform using Spherical Harmonics Transformation and UTD
abstract: This paper proposed a hybrid algorithm based on the reaction theorem to calculate the mutual coupling between two antennas with a dihedral structure platform. Directly calculate the direct electromagnetic field of the antenna at any position using the spherical harmonic transformation (SHT), through the uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) obtain the electromagnetic field of the scattered field on the sphere near the second antenna, and then get the mutual coupling through the reaction integration. The computational complexity of this new method is the same as that of the platform-free algorithm, both are O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). The comparison with MoM+UTD algorithm shows that this method is very fast, accurate, stable and universal, and it is suitable for analyzing the coupling between antennas mounted on dihedral-corner platform.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Enabled High-Resolution Localization of Non-Cooperative Wireless Source in an Indoor Environment
abstract: It is a fundamental but challenging open question to localize narrowband wireless sources in compilated indoor environment in a super-resolution and cost-efficiency way due to the complicated multipath effects. As a matter of fact, most wireless localization methods developed so far, like, the direction of arrival (DOA), received signal strength indicator (RSSI), time of arrival (TOA), etc., relies on the assumption of line-of-sight signal propagation, and fail to deal with the complicated indoor environments with the abundantly multi-path wave phenomena. To deal with the formidable challenge, we here present a super-resolution method of localizing the non-cooperative wireless sources in an indoor environment by deploying a deep-learning-driven reprogrammable metasurface and building a proof-of-principle demo system working at around 2.4GHz, where only a pair of coherent receivers are utilized for the signal acquisition. We demonstrate experimentally that our system is capable of localizing the commodity Wi-Fi signal source with an accuracy of several centimeters and a rate of 20Hz.

articleTitle: Fast Design of Millimeter-wave Bandpass Filter Using Metallic Photonic Crystal Structure
abstract: For 5G/5G beyond systems, novel platform including new transmission lines in millimeter wave as well as more efficient design methodology become inevitable. This paper presents a design of new planar bandpass filters (BPFs) using Metallic Photonic Crystal structure in millimeter wave band. A synthesis scheme based on sub-matrix provides a more efficient and fast design procedure than the traditional one. As an instant, with the proposed methodology, a direct-coupled BPF is designed and simulated. The simulated responses of the BPF agree well with the theoretical ones, which validates the proposed filter configuration and the corresponding design approach.

articleTitle: High-Dimensional Inverse Modeling Technique Using Multivalued Deep Neural Network for Parameter Extraction of Microwave Filters
abstract: This paper presents a multivalued deep neural network (DNN) inverse modeling technique and its applications in high-dimensional microwave modeling for parameter extraction of microwave filters. DNNs with smooth ReLUs have been proven to have significant abilities in dealing with complex design challenges, particularly in high-dimensional microwave forward modeling. However, for inverse modeling, the conventional DNNs with smooth ReLUs face difficulties because they cannot solve the non- uniquenessproblem which is a common and key issue in inverse modeling. In this paper, we propose a high-dimensional inverse modeling technique using multivalued DNN with smooth ReLUs to address the inverse modeling problem with high complexity and non-uniqueness issue. Finally, a more accurate DNN model can be achieved using the proposed technique compared to existing DNN modeling techniques. A high-dimensional inverse modeling example for parameter extraction of a microwave filter is presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: L-Band Multi-Channel Frequency Conversion Module With Vertical Transfer Structure
abstract: As a key part of the whole L-band RF frequency conversion system, L-band multi-channel frequency conversion module needs to meet the requirements of light weight, small volume and high integration. In order to meet the above requirements, multiple frequency conversion channels are usually integrated into one module, and the local oscillator signal of each channel is obtained by power division using the same local oscillator source. Due to the integration of multiple frequency conversion channels into one module, there will be a cross between the frequency conversion channel and the local oscillator signal. In this paper, the problem of the intermediate frequency signal generated by the frequency conversion in the multi-channel frequency conversion module is solved by the vertical output module of the intermediate frequency signal. On the basis of ensuring the function and performance of the module, the volume and weight of the multi-channel frequency conversion module are greatly reduced. Through physical production and testing, it is verified that the above design method solves the problem of the intersection of the frequency conversion signal and the local oscillator signal while ensuring the functional integrity of the multi-channel frequency conversion channel, and can greatly reduce the volume of the overall module and reduce the weight of the module.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Wide Range Parametric Modeling
abstract: The development of an electromagnetic (EM) parametric model can be challenging when the geometrical parameters of the model differ significantly. To overcome this issue, a paper reviewed an automatic system algorithm that utilizes second-order derivative information. This method involves dividing the entire geometrical region based on its degree of smoothness, creating sub-regions for both flat and uneven areas. Each sub-region's geometrical parameters are treated as variables, and a neural network model is established to represent the sub-region, which is called the sub-model. However, moving from one sub-model to an adjacent one results in a different EM response at the boundary, causing multidimensional discontinuity. The paper proposes a solution to this problem, allowing for a continuous overall model.

articleTitle: A Novel Integral Equation Method for Biperiodic Array of Connected 3-D Composite Objects
abstract: A novel periodic method of moments (PMM) in spatial time domain is proposed in this paper. By using a reasonable equivalent model and periodic Greens function (PGF), we can treat connected and disconnected biperiodic unit cells in a general way, even for complex composite structures. The example shows that the proposed method is accurate. Meanwhile, the paper provides a novel approach to reduce the calculation time of the biperiodic structure.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low Phase Noise Harmonic Shaping Class-F23 Oscillator in 65 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband low phase-noise harmonic-shaping <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Class}-\mathrm{F}_{23}$</tex> voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). The utilization of a discrete high-quality-factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Q)$</tex> multi{###} <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LC$</tex> tank in the VCO results in multiple impedance peaks under both differential mode (DM) and common mode (CM), allowing harmonic components to shape the output waveform over the wide tuning range, without the need of manual tuning. As a result, the phase noise performance can be significantly improved. For demonstration, an oscillator is implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS. The tuning range of the oscillator is from 6.52 GHz to 8.52 GHz with phase noise (PN) lower than -120.1 dBc/Hz and the figure of merit (FoM) higher than 190.3 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz frequency offset.

articleTitle: Design of Single-Layer Circularly Polarized Filtering Reflectarray Antenna
abstract: To the authors' knowledge, very few filtering reflectarray antennas have ever been reported until now. A single-layer circularly polarized filtering reflectarray antenna (CPFRA) is presented in this paper. The phase compensation element of proposed CPFRA design is adopted with a novel high frequency-selective polarization rotation reflective surface (PRRS). The phase compensation of proposed CPFRA is realized through rotating the PRRS element around with its center under illumination of circularly polarized feed antenna. The novel frequency-selective bandpass PRRS periodic element is mainly composed of a rectangular ring and the metallic ground. Especially, through the suitable coupling effect of the dual-mode resonance of the rectangular ring, a polarization conversion reflection zero can be easily introduced at the upper or lower stopband of the PRRS design. Moreover, the novel PRRS has the good merits of flexibly adjusting the location of polarization conversion reflection zero. For the verification of the proposed CPFRA design method, a prototype antenna has been presented as an example with its center frequency of 30GHz. The simulated results show that the antenna has good filtering performance, which verifies the proposed CPFRA design method.

articleTitle: A 2-18GHz Digitally Controlled Variable Gain Amplifier with Low Phase Shift and Large Dynamic Range
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband digitally controlled variable gain amplifier using 55nm CMOS technology. The VGA consists of a gain block and a digital step attenuator (DSA). The high frequency gain is compensated in the gain block and a phase compensation structure is added to the attenuator unit to reduce additional phase shift. The proposed VGA can operate from 2 to 18 GHz with a gain range of -15.5 dB to 16 dB, a 6-bit step of 0.5 dB, input and output return loss of better than 10 dB and maximum phase shift error of less than 4.3°. In maximum gain mode, the minimum noise factor is 3.9dB and IP1dB is -21dBm. The chip size is 936 × 560 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of a Four-Pole Waveguide Filter Using Derivatives-Analysis-Assisted Adjoint Neural-Network Model
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced model for microwave components using the Derivatives-Analysis-Assisted Adjoint Neural-Network (DAANN) technique. The proposed technique simultaneously trains input-output behavior of the microwave component and electromagnetic (EM) simulation derivatives to obtain a robust parametric model. Exact first and second-order derivatives of general multilayer neural-network structures are calculated to adjust the weights of DAANN, ensuring accurate output results. New formulations have been derived for the computation of second-order derivatives. The DAANN structure provides more accurate and generalized parametric models with less training data compared to existing artificial neural network (ANN) structures. This technique is demonstrated to be valid through an example of a four-pole waveguide filter.

articleTitle: A Low loss Power Combining Module for UTC-PD in the W Band
abstract: This paper proposes a power combining module for uni-travelling-carrier (UTC-PD) in the W-band, which is designed to be low loss. By using two paths for power combining and a single DC input port, the module is able to increase the overall output power. And this module can achieve low insertion loss, ranging from 0.24dB to 0.35dB in W band.

articleTitle: W-band CMOS Phased-Array Receiver with Antenna in eWLB Package
abstract: This paper presents a W-band CMOS 4-element phased-array receiver integrated with antenna in embedded wafer level ball (eWLB) package. The proposed receiver exhibits the characteristics of 5-bit gain and 7-bit phase resolution with RMS gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 0.2\text{dB}$</tex> and phase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 1^{\circ}$</tex>, respectively. Then the effects of the balun's tap on its balance and matching are investigated. To improve good balance of balun, the parasitic resistors and inductors of the input balun should be as small as possible. Meanwhile, short-circuited stub is also added onto the output balun to realize good output impedance matching. Finally, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times4$</tex> array in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{eWLB}$</tex> package with wide beam steering of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 40^{\circ}$</tex> is realized in this work.

articleTitle: A Normalization Method for Unified Near-Field and Far-Field Localization
abstract: An improved normalization method for unified near- field and far-field localization is proposed. The localization problem could be solved in the modification polar coordinate system (MPR) by firstly linearizing the nonlinear equations and using the weighted least squares (WLS) to obtain a coarse solution, then the coarse solution is tightened by a new constraint about the correlation between signals. The simulation results show that the proposed method could achieve a more efficient result compared with the traditional unified localization methods.

articleTitle: Transient Electromagnetic Simulation for Periodic Structures with a Modified Parallel DGTD Method
abstract: Due to natural block diagonal mass matrices, discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method provides convenient condition for parallel computation. However, when the number of processes increases, the traffic between processes gradually increases, leading to the sharp decline of the parallelism efficiency. To solve these problems, non-blocking communication technology with the math kernel library (MKL) scheme is proposed to improve the efficiency of message passing interface (MPI) parallel computing. Thus, a typical periodic electromagnetic structure - frequency selective surface (FSS) is simulated, which achieves an acceleration ratio of more than 1.8 times, and further improves the performance of the DGTD algorithm.

articleTitle: A Flexible Miniature RFID Tag Based on Planar Microstrip Antenna for Strain Measurement on Metal Surface
abstract: In this paper, a flexible and miniaturized RFID strain sensor tag with chip is proposed for the detection of metal surface strain. The flexible miniature RFID tag is composed of a flexible substrate, tag microstrip antenna and RF chip. Its flexible substrate and small size makes it suitable for more application scenarios and reduces the cost of a single tag. The flexible RFID sensor tag is designed and the parameters are optimized firstly. Then, the strain detection performance of the tag is studied through numerical simulation. Finally, a quantitative detection approach of metal surface strain is proposed, which can realize the quantitative nondestructive and wireless detection for the metal component surface strain. The designed RFID strain sensor are expected to be applied in the surface strain monitoring for the bearing in the EEF bogie of the high-speed train as well as the interlaminar stress in hydrogen storage tank as well.

articleTitle: A CORDIC-based Multi-Scene MIMO Channel Emulator
abstract: In this paper, a non-stationary multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel model suitable for fixed-point implementation on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) hardware platform is proposed, and a scalable hardware architecture is developed. On this basis, an improved CORDIC method is proposed to realize complex exponent operation, which reduces the computational complexity and hardware resource consumption. The measured results show that the probability density function (PDF) of the simulated output channel fading is in good agreement with the theoretical value, the hardware resource utilization rate is reduced from 6.61% to 3.51%, and the delay time is reduced by 10 clock cycles.

articleTitle: Analytical Derivations and Coefficients Between 1-dB/3-dB and Ripple-Bandwidths for Chebyshev Filtering Responses
abstract: Analytical expressions between 1-dB/3-dB and ripple-bandwidths for classical Chebyshev responses are derived for the first time since ripple-bandwidths are generally required in filter synthesis while 1-dB/3-dB bandwidths are usually designated in specifications or post-circuit designs. Based on the derived expressions, coefficients for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>th-order (n ∊ [1], [10]) Chebyshev filtering responses are computed and tabulated with three critical cases synthesized for validations. Finally, a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order Chebyshev-type bandpass filter based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is synthesized, designed, fabricated, and measured as a practical demonstration and verification.

articleTitle: Biorthogonal Circularly Polarized OAM Wave Generation Based on a Miniaturized High-Efficiency Holographic Impedance Surface
abstract: In this paper, based on impedance superposition algorithm, we propose a miniaturized and efficient holographic impedance surface that generates biorthogonal circularly polarized OAM beams. By means of a circular anisotropic element with a cross slit and the derived holographic impedance tensor impedance modulation formula, a holographic impedance surface capable of generating biorthogonal circular-polarized OAM beams along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=\mathbf{3 0}, \varphi=0^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=30^{\circ}, \varphi=180^{\circ}$</tex> at 14. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\mathbf{GHz}$</tex> is designed. The results show that the designed holographic impedance surface can stably generate biorthogonal circular-polarized OAM beams with an aperture efficiency of 25.5%. Compared with other OAM-generating holographic impedance surfaces, it has the advantages of miniaturization and high efficiency, which provides a reference for wireless communication of multiplex and multitarget radar detection.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Folded Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Transmission Line
abstract: This letter presents a miniaturized folded spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) transmission line (TL). The proposed TL has two substrate layers and three metal layers. It includes the U-shaped groove on the surface of the top substrate, the folding branch on the middle metal layer, and the metalized blind vias connecting the U-shaped groove and the folding branch. Compared with the conventional U-shaped SSPP TL, the metallized vias and the folded branch extend the current path and result in the small lateral width. The folded SSPP TL is fabricated under PCB process. The experimental results demonstrate that the operating bandwidth of the proposed TL is 0–12 GHz and its lateral width is reduced by 56% compared with the conventional U-shaped SSPP.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Compact Range Reflectors with Arbitrary Rolled Edges
abstract: A method to optimize rolled edges for compact range reflectors is presented. The reflectors may be center-fed or offset-fed. For arbitrary shaped reflectors with arbitrary rolled edges, the proposed method can obtain an excellent performance without changing the projection of the reflector. A procedure to optimize reflectors with rolled edges is also presented. An example is treated in order to prove the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Simulation of Sea Clutter Based on Space-Time-Coding Digital Metasurfaces
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the current land-based sea scene simulation techniques, which struggle to balance dynamic simulations, coupling effects, large areas, and construction costs, we present a novel single-station simulation method for studying the electromagnetic responses of highly dynamic sea surfaces based on space-time-coding digital metasurfaces, in which a new binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) algorithm is used to optimize coding sequence, making the technique have higher optimization efficiency. We verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach by designing the coding sequence corresponding to Weibull and Rayleigh distributions of sea clutters. The simulation results indicate that our method can effectively and accurately imitate the backscatter coefficient distributions of sea clutters under excitations of monochromatic waves.

articleTitle: On-Chip CPW Low-Pass Filter with 50–110 GHz Bandstop in 400 nm Metal Thickness Technology Towards Lab-Level Ka-Band MMICs
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave low-pass filter to investigate the RF performance of passive structures in a lab-level thin metal micro-nano processing technology. It consists of 3-stage periodic stepped-impedance cell to have a slow-wave structure to offer a high attenuation of stop band with a compact size. The total size of the chip is less than 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It achieves an insertion loss of less than 2 dB at a frequency range from 0 to 110 GHz with a measured cut-off frequency around 40 GHz. A rejection of higher than 20 dB is measured in a stopband from 52 to 110 GHz, which is larger than 2 times of fundamental frequency. The measurement agrees well with the simulation results. It shows the potential of RF passives in a lab-level thinner metal thickness technology towards monolithic microwave integrated circuits.

articleTitle: A Receiver Reconfigurable Method for Indoor Human Detection with 60GHz MIMO FMCW Radar
abstract: A new receiver (Rx) reconfigurable method is proposed to enhance the target signal. After theoretical derivation and experimental verification, the proposed method solves the problem of poor signal-to-signal ratio (SNR) when using 60GHz MIMO FMCW radar for indoor positioning. The proposed method combines multiple original Rx channel data to form a new data channel, forming a new virtual antenna array. This method improves the SNR of the echo signal without affecting the estimation of the target angle. In the scenarios where the human body is standing or sitting, the SNR is improved by more than 28dB. The new data matrix is used to resolve the angle. Due to the improved target strength, the angle resolution accuracy is also improved compared with the traditional single Rx channel

articleTitle: Design of a W-Band Band-Stop Cavity Filter Based on Multi-Mode Resonator
abstract: In this paper, a band-stop resonant cavity is designed based on the characteristics of transmission zeros generated by mutual suppression between different resonant modes in a multi-mode resonant cavity. By optimizing the size of the multi-mode resonant cavity, the position of the two transmission zeros generated by the two pairs of resonant modes is adjusted, and a band-stop resonant cavity with a stopband of 90.5 GHz-94.77 GHz is designed. Based on the band-stop resonator designed by the multi-mode resonator, a band-stop cavity filter with a band-stop band-width of 6.95 GHz (89.16GHz ~ 96.11 GHz) is designed by cascading and differentiating the two band-stop resonators.

articleTitle: Generation of Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Orbital Angular Momentum Beams with Holographic Impedance Metasurface
abstract: This paper presents a method that can independently modulate dual-polarized Orbit Angular Momentum (OAM) beams in dual bands. The holographic impedance metasurface consists of 30*30 unit cells with both scalar and tensor impedance properties, the generation of beams in different frequency bands can be controlled independently by modulating different parameters. A right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) OAM beam is generated at 11.2GHz, with a gain of 18.03dBi, an aperture efficiency of 14.93%, and a vortex beam purity of 90%. Two linearly polarized (LP) OAM beams are generated at 18.2GHz, with a gain of 18.16dBi, an aperture efficiency of 23.3%, and a purity of the vortex beam is 85.4% and 83% respectively.

articleTitle: A Compact and High Selectivity Bandpass Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Technology
abstract: A compact and high selectivity bandpass filter (BPF) consisting of parallel-coupled three-line (PCTL) units and shorted stubs is proposed using substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) technology. Single via transitions are adopted to connect the BPF with the grounded coplanar waveguides (GCPWs). Moreover, an equivalent circuit model is built to understanding the properties of the BPF. Two transmission zeros (TZs) are created by the shorted stubs and the gap between the PCTL units. The locations of the TZs are closed to the passband edges of the proposed BPF as the gap capacitance increased and the electrical length of the shorted stubs decreased, so a compact size and high selectivity can be obtained. Finally, a BPF prototype is fabricated by PCB process and the results indicate that the proposed BPF centered at 25.9 GHz is realized with compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.42\lambda_{g}\times 0.28\lambda_{g}$</tex> and high selectivity factor of 0.554, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{g}$</tex> is the wavelength at 25.9 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of FBAR/IPD/MMIC chips for 5G applications
abstract: This invited talk firstly presents a compact low-loss high-selectivity excellent-isolation duplexer chip for LTE Band-3 industrial applications based on the film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) technology. At present, the FBAR technology is mainly used for bands of the fourth generation (4G). As the frequency of signal increases, there is transverse acoustic leakage, resulting in filter performance degradation. This talk also introduces a highselectivity FABR filter chip in 3.4-3.6 GHz, which shows the potentiality of the applications of FBAR for 5G. FBAR technology also has its own limitations, when the frequency continues to rise to 5G millimeter-wave band. Integrated passive device (IPD) technology can be used as an alternative of FBAR to realize millimeterwave filters. In the implementation of amplifiers, monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) technology is the main technology.

articleTitle: A 24.25-29.5GHz 32-Element Integrated Phased-Array Antenna Based on a Scalable $4\times 4$ Antenna-in-Package Array Cell
abstract: This article presents a dual-polarized (+45 ° pol/- 45 °pol) 32-element integrated phased-array antenna, covering 3GPP 5G NR2 N258 / N257 bands (i.e., 24.25-29.5 GHz) based on the scalable 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4$</tex> antenna-in-package (AiP) array cell. The standard AiP array is based on the silicon-based CMOS phased- array ICs with 6-bit amplitude/phase control. By adopting the fan-out wafer level chip scale packaging (WLCSP) technology and the low-cost high-frequency multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB) integrated antenna methodologies, this work achieves the measured effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of over 47.3 dBm across 24.25G-29.5 GHz. When the dual- polarized antenna achieves a large scanned angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> (azimuth plane) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> (elevation plane), the gain is degraded by 4.2 dB and 2.6 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-band Filter Based on Separate Electric and Magnetic Coupling Paths Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band dual-path BPF based on the separate electric and magnetic coupling paths (SEMCPs) technology. Each single-path consists of a half-wavelength UIR resonator and two quarter-wavelength SIR resonators. By adjusting the equivalent capacitive element and equivalent inductive element between the SIR resonators, the mixed coupling can be equivalently separated to a magnetic coupling path and an electric coupling path, then the TZs of the proposed filter can be controllable. This topology can not only realize the controllable filter TZs, but also has the advantages of high selectivity and miniaturization.

Author Keywords: separate electric and magnetic coupling paths

articleTitle: A 94-GHz SiGe Power Amplifier With 18.5 dB Power Gain and 14.4 dBm PSAT
abstract: A fully integrated two-stage differential power amplifier (PA) for 92-96-GHz applications in 130-nm silicon germanium (SiGe) technology is presented in this paper. A practical technique based on series capacitor at the base of the differential cascode structure is applied to enhance the stability and gain of the differential cascode cell. Transformer-based input and output matching networks play a role in impedance transformation and turn the differential input and output ends of the circuit into single-end. Compact metal-oxide-metal (MOM) capacitors are employed to implement inter-stage matching network. The proposed PA achieves a simulated power gain of 18.5 dB at 94 GHz and it's 3-dB gain bandwidth is 20 GHz from 81 GHz to 101 GHz. Moreover, the PA obtains a saturated output power of 14.4 dBm and maximum power-added efficiency (PAE) of 10.5% at 94 GHz. The area of the entire layout is 0.462 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the core area is only 0.032 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of a Directly-Fed Pattern Reconfigurable Patch Antenna and Its Array Performance
abstract: A directly-fed pattern reconfigurable patch antenna without extra feeding networks is presented in this paper with a straightforward design method and the discussion on its array performance. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{T}\mathrm{M}_{01}$</tex> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> modes of a rectangular patch are employed to realize pattern reconfigurability. Four shorting pins underneath the patch and two high-impedance open-ended stubs loaded on the radiating edges are adopted for the frequency overlap of the two working modes. Additional center-carved slots or center-loaded stubs are proposed as a simple impedance-matching mechanism without feeding networks. The working principle is investigated by a transmission-line circuit model. Simulation results show that at 2.45 GHz, the radiation pattern of the proposed antenna can be switched between a single beam and dual beams with maximum realized gains of 9.6 dBi and 5.6 dBi, respectively. Moreover, a 1×4 array is designed using the proposed antenna to demonstrate its array performance.

articleTitle: A Tunable Metamaterial Element Based on Liquid Crystals for Holographic Beam-Steering Antennas
abstract: This work presents an electronically reconfigurable metamaterial element based on liquid crystals operating in Ka- Band. The proposed metamaterial element features a continuously tunable transmission coefficient, which can be applied to control the magnitude of the local aperture field. As the electrodes are electrical isolated with each other, individual biasing is realized. The element size is relatively small compared with the wavelength, which provides a fine sampling of the reference wave. By allocating the metamaterial elements with specific biasing voltages, the desired aperture field and thus the directional beam can be formed. The proposed structure is easy to be integrated into common guiding wave structures. Measured results show that the resonant frequency continuously shifts from 28.5 GHz to 26.1 GHz when the addressing voltage varies from 2.5 V to 10 V. A fast response time of around 150 ms was achieved with a thin liquid crystal layer of around 11.2 um.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Flexible Terahertz Sensor Based on Rotated Metamaterial Structure
abstract: In this article, a terahertz flexible metamaterial sensor with dual-band operating characteristics is introduced. The gold metamaterial array is arranged on the top surface of a polyimide film, while the structure is made up of a rotated structure with spiral-shaped strips. Two resonances occur at 0.37 and 1.13 THz with outstanding polarization insensitivity. The metamaterial sensor also has sensitive refractive index sensing properties, with sensitivities of 0.1 THz/RIU and 0.3 THz/RIU, respectively, at the two operating bands. This work shows potential applications in refractive index and nesticide sensing.

articleTitle: A 23-29.5 GHz Differential Power Amplifier in a 45-nm SOI CMOS Technology for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: A 23-29.5 GHz differential power amplifier (PA) implemented in a 45-nm silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS technology for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-wave) application is presented. The PA adopts a two-stage differential configuration based on baluns and a transformer which offer highly flexible and efficient matching networks with minimized area occupancy. A two-stacked FET topology is used for the output stage to realize high output power (Pout). The proposed PA achieves a peak gain of 26.3 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth of 6.5 GHz for 23- 29.5 GHz. At 26 GHz, the simulated saturated output power (Psat), 1-dB output compression point (P1dB), and peak power- added efficiency (PAE) are 20.4 dBm, 18.5 dBm, and 31.1%, respectively.

articleTitle: A 220-GHz High Linearity Power Amplifier with 25.7-dB Gain and 9.7-dB PSAT
abstract: In this brief, a 220-GHz power amplifier (PA) utilizing a three-stage differential cascode (CC) configuration is presented. The PA employs the gm-boosting technique and a ladder-type interconnection method to enhance gain and output power in 0.13-µm SiGe BiCMOS process. To achieve better performance, it utilizes modified Marchand baluns (MBLs) with metal-oxide-metal (MOM) capacitors instead of transformer-based baluns (TBLs) for signal transformation from single-ended to differential (S2D). Simulated results demonstrate that this PA presents a peak gain of 25.8 dB at 217 GHz, PAE of 1.9%, and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</inf> /OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> up to 9.7/7.7 dBm within the bandwidth. Compared to other silicon-based differential PAs operating above 210 GHz, this circuit shows excellent linearity, with 1-dB compression point 2 dB less than saturation.

articleTitle: Liquid Metal-Based Linear Self-Complementary Phase Shifter for Phased Array Antenna
abstract: This paper proposes a liquid metal (LM)-based linear tunable phase shifter. A via-pad-slot (VPS) structure is realized by using a slot to isolate a via from the ground. The shunt inductance and capacitance are loaded on the HMSIW when the VPS structure is inserted in the HMSIW. While the capacitance will be removed when the square slot is filled by LM. The shunt inductance and capacitance have complementary phase effect which causes a small phase deviation with frequency. According to the proposed VPS structure, a X-band linear tunable HMSIW phase shifter range is 0-100° when the slots are sequentially filled by LM. The measured insertion loss (IL) is 0.85 dB, the phase shift ranges from 0 to 100° within 9.5-13 GHz (31.11%), and the average phase resolution is about 1.79°. The phase shifter offers benefits such as low insertion loss, high resolution, linear phase adjustment, and negligible phase deviation, which is attractive to passive phased array antenna design

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Cost and Low-Loss DS-GWG Solution using Advanced Glass Packages at V-Band
abstract: This paper presents a novel low-loss and low-cost double-sided gap waveguide (DS-GWG) fabricated by glass packaging process for V-band applications. The proposed structure is stacked with three layers of inexpensive glass substrates utilizing a dry film bonding process. The middle layer is distributed with a large number of electromagnetic band gap (EBG) units, composed of double-sided metal rings and non-vertical through glass vias (TGV), to prevent the leakage of the electro-magnetic wave within the gap. Most of the glass in the transmission area is removed by the laser-induced wet etching (LIWE) process to achieve low transmission loss. Its excellent transmission performance has been verified by simulation and measurement in the V-band. The measured transmission loss is as low as 0.02 dB/mm, exhibiting an outstanding low-loss performance. Moreover, the newly proposed glass-substrate-based DS-GWG solution behaves at low cost and low loss, and it is very suitable for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A Broadband Terahertz Circular Polarization Selective Surface
abstract: This paper introduces a novel wideband circular polarization selective surface (CPSS) design operating at terahertz (THz) frequencies. The proposed right-hand CPSS can reflect the right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) electromagnetic waves while transmitting the left-hand circularly polarized (LCHP) ones. The CPSS consists of three metallic grating layers separated by SU8 substrates without any vias interconnection. The proposed structure combines two linear-to-circular polarization converters sharing the same linear grating polarizer, substantially reducing the required number of metallic layers.
