Measured results show that the proposed CPSS presents a wide bandwidth of 57% with a transmission CP discrimination of more than 15 dB from 0.6 THz to 1.08 THz.

articleTitle: A Novel Load Modulated Power Amplifier for Extending High Efficiency Power Range
abstract: To extend the high efficiency power range (HEPR) of the power amplifier (PA), a novel load-modulated PA (LMPA) architecture is proposed in this paper. The proposed LMPA consists of a Doherty PA (DPA) and a balanced PA (PA). The output signal of the DPA is delivered into the isolation port of the output coupler of the BPA, which is in class-C mode. The DPA has a local load modulation because it is connected to the isolation port of the output coupler. The proposed LMPA can extend the HEPR greatly due to the local modulated DPA has a 6 dB HEPR. Based on the proposed architecture, a LMPA operating at 1.95 GHz is implemented in this paper. Experimental results show the maximum output power of the fabricated LMPA is 45.7 dBm. And the saturation and 13 dB back-off drain efficiencies (DEs) are 62% and 47%, respectively. Meantime, the fabricated LMPA achieves DEs of 49% and 50% at the output back-off power levels of 6 and 9 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Study on the Propagation Characteristic Prediction of Clustering Algorithms for V2V Time-Varying Channel
abstract: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is the application of mobile communication technology in the field of intelligent transportation, which can realize real-time information interaction, and the vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) technology provides solutions for driverless and intelligent traffic planning. In order to analyze time-varying channels, it is necessary to characterize the evolution characteristics of multipath component (MPC). In this paper, a cluster-based tracking and prediction method for time-varying channels is proposed to improve the accuracy of cluster identification and prediction in time-varying channels. Firstly, the channel parameters of V2V time-varying channel are clustered based on K-means. Then, Kuhn-Munkres (K-M) algorithm is used to track and identify clusters while characterize the evolution process of the clusters. Finally, a prediction method based on Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) to predict the tracking trajectory of clusters is proposed, and the effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation in a typical dense urban. The results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of the results compared with the traditional method for predicting clusters. Therefore, the proposed method in this paper has better performance for the identification and prediction of dynamic clusters in V2V time-varying channels.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Balanced Bandpass Filter Chip Using Lumped-element Based on IPD Technology
abstract: In this paper, a novel miniaturized balanced band-pass filter (BPF) chip using lumped-element is proposed. First, the balanced BPF is analyzed by using transformation formulas between ABCD matrix and Sparameters. The filter chip is designed and fabricated based on integrated passive device (IPD) technology. Finally, measured results show that differential-mode (DM) return loss is higher than 10.5 dB, DM insertion loss in band ranges from 2.453 to 2.813 dB and common-mode (CM) suppression from 0 to 6.5 GHz is better than 21 dB. The size of the filter based on IPD technology is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.015 \times 1.170\text{mm}^{2}$</tex> •

articleTitle: Intelligent Imaging and Sensing based on Programmable Metasurface
abstract: Recently, electromagnetic (EM) sensing has been rapidly applied to many areas like science, health and military, working in a all-weather and all-day way without invasion of visual privacy. In order to tackle the data crisis of traditional EM sensing algorithms, we propose an intelligent metasurface sensing system by synergizing the programmable metasurface for flexible wave manipulation on physical level and artificial intelligence for powerful computation on data level. The integrated sensor can jointly learn the optimal settings of data acquisition and processing and achieves excellent performance on a variety of indoor imaging and detection tasks. The reported work could pave a new avenue for future smart homes and healthy monitoring.

articleTitle: Phased Array Antenna with Polarization Diversity and Frequency Diversity for the 5G/6G Mobile Base Station
abstract: Polarization diversity and frequency diversity have been proven to be very efficient and useful in high multipath environments and frequency selective channel environments among all antenna diversity techniques. A tile architecture of the phased array antenna (PAA) with polarization diversity and frequency diversity at the same time for the 5G/6G mobile base station is presented in this paper. The system structure, the array arrangement, and the simulation model are introduced and the radiation patterns of the PAA with different polarization in the S-Band and in the C-band are described, respectively. The simulation results show that the presented antenna has excellent performance.

articleTitle: Sub-Thz Multibeams Shaping Metasurface Based on Circular Polarization Decoupled Meta-Atom
abstract: With the advent of the 5G era, the rapid depletion of spectrum resources has led researchers to focus on multifunctional devices operating in the millimeter-wave range. On the other hand, circular polarization also attracts considerable attention due to its unique advantages. To this end, this study proposes a shared aperture metasurface based on a circular polarization decoupled metasurface. By controlling both the circular polarization state of the transmitted wave and the linear polarization state of the incident wave, this metasurface allows independent control of four circularly polarized beams, enabling a variety of novel functions. To validate the feasibility of this approach, a metasurface was designed to deflect four beams with a center frequency of 110 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of 18.2%. Simulation results show excellent performance, in line with expectations.

articleTitle: A Composite Absorber of FSS and Area-coated Honeycomb Using High-loss Materials for Broadband Applications
abstract: In this article, a novel composite absorber of an area-coated honeycomb (ACH) and frequency selective surface (FSS) for broadband applications is theoretically and experimentally investigated. The characteristic of this structure is to broaden the bandwidth of the absorber by introducing ACH into FSS absorber. And the absorption of electromagnetic waves is enhanced by using high loss materials in coated honeycomb. The principle of using high-loss materials, multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT), in the coated honeycomb to enhance electromagnetic waves absorption is also analyzed from the perspective of input admittance. The designed absorber possesses a -10 dB fractional absorption bandwidth of 154.8% from 2.05 GHz to 15.70 GHz, and it has a thickness of 0.113 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex> is the wavelength at the lowest frequency. Reflectivity measurements were basically consistent with calculated values, validating the design principle and preparation technique for the composite.

articleTitle: The feasibility of Q-band millimeter wave on hand-gesture recognition for indoor FTTR scenario
abstract: The generalization for different scenarios and different users is an urgent problem for millimeter wave gesture recognition for indoor fiber-to-the-room (FTTR) scenario. In order to solve this problem and verify the feasibility of FTTR Q-band millimeter wave in gesture recognition, we build a real-time millimeter wave gesture recognition system. The moving hand-gestures are represented as a variety of time-variant spectrum features, such as micro- Doppler feature, and then the feature learning and classification is realized by using a convolution neural network (CNN). The experimental results show that the millimeter wave gesture recognition system can achieve the generalized gesture recognition for 2 scenarios and 4 users.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent Reflective Metasurface for Wireless Energy Transmission
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optically transparent reflective metasurface based on indium tin oxide (ITO) with a sheet impedance of 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\Omega}/\mathbf{sq}$</tex>. The metasurface unit parameters are analyzed and optimized to solve the balance between antenna loss and light propagation characteristics, and by analyzing and optimizing the parameters of the metasurface unit, the balance between antenna loss and optical transmission characteristics is solved, and high reflection efficiency and wide phase shift curve range are optimized to achieve a wide phase shift range of nearly 350° The designed unit works at 5.8 GHz, and a non-diffraction zero-order Bessel beam is generated based on a transparent metasurface composed of such units. By performing simulation in HFSS, the high performance of the unit designed in this work is verified. The results show that the transparent metasurface composed of the designed unit can be used for wireless power transfer or reception in light wave transmission environment.

articleTitle: Optimization of 60 GHz three-port Grid Array Antenna
abstract: This paper proposes optimization methods for a 60GHz three-port Grid Array Antenna (GAA), aiming to opti-mize the return loss and Gain of the antenna. The working frequency range of the antenna is 57GHz~64GHz. After optimization, the GAA produces frequency scanning beams with 1~2 dB Gain improvement when feeding at edge ports and boresight resonant beams with 2dB Gain improvement when feeding at the center port with Return Loss >11dB. The feature of frequency scanning and boresight resonant beams produced by this three-port GAA will find usage in 2D and 3D multi-mood Radar imaging applications.

articleTitle: A 6-18GHz 10W GaN Balanced Power Amplifier MMIC
abstract: A 6-18GHz 10W GaN balanced power amplifier (BPA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) is demonstrated in this paper. The BPA architecture with mis-matched load impedance is analyzed to reveal its anti-mismatch characteristic. And then, two reactively matched power amplifi-ers and Lange couplers are adopted to construct the ultra-wideband BPA. The final fabricated PA MMIC achieves a satu-rated output power of 10W, a PAE of 19%-34% and a small sig-nal gain of larger than 20dB. Both the input and output return loss are better than -15dB across the whole band, which makes the PA more reliable when cascaded with poorly matched components such as ultra-wideband switches or antennas.

articleTitle: A 70-80 GHz Image Rejection Resistive Mixer using 0.1um GaAs pHEMT Technology
abstract: This paper presents a MMIC image rejection resistive mixer in 70–80 GHz frequency range. The WIN (WIN Semi-conductors Corp.) 0.1 um GaAs pHEMT technology provides W-band high performance FET under high power. The mixer uses Hartley topology and takes advantage of the high linearity of the resistive cold-FET. Within 70–80 GHz, the input third-order inter-modulation point (IIP3) is higher than 21 dBm and the conversion loss is lower than 11.9 dB. The LO-RF isolation is higher than 30 dB above 72GHz and the image rejection ratio is above 20 dBc.

articleTitle: A DE/WD/VM Hybrid Algorithm for Multiple-Constraint Synthesis of Concentric Ring Arrays
abstract: a hybrid synthesis algorithm is proposed by combining differential evolutionary (DE) algorithm with weighting density (WD) method and vector mapping (VM) method to synthesize the radiation pattern of concentric ring arrays (CRAs) with multiple constraints. The constraints in the optimization process mainly include the total number of elements, the size of the array and the minimum spacing between the elements. Both numerical example and full wave simulation are presented to verify the effectiveness and stability of the proposed DE/WD/VM hybrid algorithm.

articleTitle: Highly Integrated Multi-Channel RF Front-End Module
abstract: As the most front-end part of the frequency conversion system, the RF front-end module undertakes the function of amplifying the RF signal. The RF front-end part includes the self-checking power dividing function. The self-checking power dividing function is to divide the self-checking signal into each channel and provide the self-checking signal for each channel. In this paper, by selecting the integrated power divider, the self-test power divider circuit is integrated on the back control circuit board of the RF front-end module. The self-test power divider circuit on the back of the module is interconnected with the front RF circuit through the RF insulator, which effectively reduces the volume and weight of the RF front-end module and improves the integration of the module.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Path Loss Prediction Across Multiple Frequency Bands using a Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Model
abstract: As a large-scale channel parameter, the path loss is important in the deployment and optimization of wireless networks. The introduction of machine learning brings convenience to path loss prediction, but the amount of data required for training increases the workload of channel measurement. First, based on machine learning, a multi-fidelity path loss prediction model across multiple frequency bands is introduced. Then, the existing low-frequency channel data is used as the prior knowledge to generate low-fidelity high-frequency channel data. Next, combining with a small amount of high-fidelity high-frequency measurement data, the path loss prediction accuracy is improved while the high-fidelity training data is greatly reduced. Finally, the results show that the multi-fidelity model can get close to the general machine learning model, the prediction error is 3.73 dB, but the number of samples is reduced by 80%.

articleTitle: Novel Shuffle Algorithm for Efficient Training of Neuron Network Digital Predistortion
abstract: This paper presents a shuffle algorithm to optimize the training sequence for the stochastic and the mini-batch training of neuron network (NN) digital predistortion (DPD) technique. The proposed training sequence can ensure an efficient convergence by reducing the correlation of continuous inputs. Experiments are validated through an augmented real-valued time-delay neural network (ARVTDNN). Experiment results show that the proposed training sequence can significantly improve the convergence speeds and the linearization performance.

articleTitle: ELF Electromagnetic Wave Across Sea Level from HED in Three-layered Medium
abstract: Exploring the electromagnetic wave propagation in the marine environment is extremely important in ship communication and marine information monitoring. Understanding the propagation law of electromagnetic waves in the marine environment plays a theoretical guiding role in the application related to the propagation of electromagnetic waves. This paper discusses the influence of the seabed medium in the stratified marine environment on the electromagnetic field in the air radiated from the low-frequency horizontal electric dipole (HED) located at the seawater. The conclusion shows that the existence of seabed media will affect the magnitude of electromagnetic field amplitude on the sea surface, but will not change the law of electromagnetic wave propagation in the air except different field intensity.

articleTitle: A 10–17 GHz 25W GaN Power Amplifier MMIC Using Asymmetric Active Impedance
abstract: A broadband monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) is presented based on the asymmetric active impedance matching network, which is manufactured in 0.20 μm gallium nitride (GaN) process. Compared to traditional design, the impedance of transistor cells is transformed to suitable impedance, and then synthesized to the output impedance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{Z}_{\mathbf{output}})$</tex>, rather than directly transformed to 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex>, breaking the bandwidth limitation of the order of output match network (OMN). The PA assessment findings indicated a power added efficiency (PAE) up to 29% over 10–17 GHz with an typical output power of 44 dBm at a drain voltage of 28 V. The chip size is 4 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4.1$</tex> mm.

articleTitle: Phased Array Fed Reflector Antenna for OAM-Generating and Beam-Scanning Applications
abstract: This paper shows the design concept of a reflector antenna with a small Vivaldi array feed antenna. The proposed design is employed for launching angular momentum (OAM) beams, as well as beam scanning applications. In the design procedure, the working mechanisms of the Vivaldi array fed-reflector are discussed firstly. Then, the design details of the Vivaldi array feed are analyzed, followed by the discussions of multi-mode OAM beams and scanning beam radiation patterns. Thanks to the inherent multi-beam abilities of the reflector, the 0-OAM-mode beam can be steered over a conical scanning range of ±10°. Moreover, the flexible excitations of the Vivaldi array feed provide more possibilities to superpose multiple OAM states simultaneously, which can enhance the spectrum efficiency and the channel capacity.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz Power Amplifier Based on Broadband Adaptive Linearization Technique in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: A 28 GHz linear power amplifier (PA) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{G}$</tex> multiband application is proposed in this paper. Based on the proposed broadband adaptive linearization technique, properly designed inter-stage power splitting network, and output power combining network, the P A has broadband linearization performance improvement and high power-added efficiency (P AE) within the operating frequency band. The proposed PA is implemented in 65-nm CMOS process and exhibits a 3-dB bandwidth of S21 from 21.5 to 33 GHz, covering n257/n258/n261 bands. The PA shows maximum power gain of 23.3 dB with output 1-dB compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{P}_{1\text{dB}})$</tex>, saturation output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{P}_{\text{sat}})$</tex>, and peak P AE of 24.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dBm},\ 24.9\ \text{dBm}$</tex>, and 31.8% at 28 GHz, respectively. The 1-dB bandwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_{1\text{dB}}$</tex> is from 21.8 to 35.2 GHz with corresponding PAE exceeding 22%.

articleTitle: A Ultra-Wideband Slot Directional Coupler Based on S-ISCGW
abstract: A novel lantern-coupled microstrip 90° millimeter-wave ultra-wideband directional coupler based on symmetrically integrated substrate-coupled gap waveguide (S-ISCGW) is proposed. The directional coupler consists of a vertically symmetrical ISCGW, in which the lantern-coupled transmission line is coupled through a hexagonal coupling groove located on a common ground plane. The simulation results show that the band-width range of the directional coupler is 23.32~29.97 GHz, the relative bandwidth is 25%, the return loss is less than -20dB, the average isolation of the whole operating frequency band is greater than 26.5 dB, and a flat coupling of 3±0.35dB is obtained. The phase difference between the through port and the coupling port is 90°±0.46°.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Mode-Composite Leaky-Wave Antenna
abstract: A novel leaky-wave antenna is proposed. The antenna is fed by a mode-composite waveguide supporting the single quasi-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode in the two individual bands. Periodic transverse slots with a simple geometry that are introduced to the broad wall of the waveguide are employed as the radiation structure. The constructed prototype demonstrates that forward-scanning radiation beams in the low frequency of 8.7–10.4 GHz and in the high frequency of 26–35 GHz, respectively. Burgeoning dual-band wireless devices that operate in both millimeter-wave and microwave bands can benefit from the proposed leaky-wave antenna.

articleTitle: Active Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Integrated with Thin-Film Schottky Barrier Diodes at Millimeter Wave and Terahertz Frequencies
abstract: In this paper, metal-oxide thin-film Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) are proposed to dynamically manipulate spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) at millimeter wave (MMW) and terahertz (THz) frequencies. Bridging the gaps of split ring resonators (SRRs) and electric-field-coupled inductor-capacitor resonators (ELCRs) with planar thin-film SBD structure can actively change the thin-film carrier density within the gaps via forward bias, which manipulates the resonant amplitude of SSPPs at central frequencies consequently. As a demonstration, single-frequency and dual-frequency active SSPP devices with SRRs were fabricated and tested, showing an excellent amplitude modulation and dual-frequency multi-bit modulation capability at MMW frequencies, respectively. Furthermore, the planar thin-film SBD structure was integrated in an ELCR array to verify the feasibility of the proposed modulation method at 0.39 THz. This method greatly promotes the working frequency of the metal-oxide thin-film SBDs, and pave a new way for program-mable SSPPs at MMW and THz frequencies.

articleTitle: An Adaptive RFIC Layout Generator with DRC Violations Self-repair Strategy
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive layout generator for RFIC, by disassembling the prototype layout geometries into lines and blocks, specifying the corresponding variables on top of them, and finally mapping them to the modification of the proto-type layout. In addition, the DRC violations self-repair strategy including spacing adaptive repair and automatic jumper generation is integrated into this layout generator, resulting in a much higher DRC pass rate. Compared to the conventional Pcell technique, the modelling process of the proposed method is less time-consuming, and it supports work migration across technology nodes,making it more flexible and convenient for design.

articleTitle: Developing a THz subharmonic-spectrometer for lunar water analysis
abstract: The design of a THz subharmonic-spectrometer typically involves the use of a frequency multiplier chain to generate the desired THz frequency range. The spectrometer would also require a highly sensitive detector capable of measuring the small changes in the THz signal caused by the presence of water molecules. One possible approach to detect water on the moon is to use a THz subharmonic-spectrometer on board a lunar orbiter or lander. The spectrometer would scan the lunar surface and measure the THz signal, looking for any changes that may indicate the presence of water. The data collected by the spectrometer could then be used to create a map of the lunar surface and identify potential areas where water may be present. Our paper presents a novel approach to detect water on the moon using a 183GHz subharmonic-spectrometer. Our design incorporates a smooth-walled horn antenna to receive signals and an Arduino-based PLL multiplier frequency to generate local oscillator signals for subharmonic mixing. By utilizing this technology, we aim to improve the sensitivity and accuracy of water detection on the lunar surface.

articleTitle: Design of Triple-Resonance Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna with Double Cavities
abstract: In this paper, a triple-resonance substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna (CBSA) with double cavities is proposed. The antenna is divided into double cavities by loading a symmetrical row of shorting vias. The double cavities and non-resonant slot help to influence current distributions that excite a lower mode (half-TE110) and two higher modes (odd and even TE210). Reflection coefficients of the three frequency points are affected by the dimensions of the cavities and the slot. A prototype is measured which exhibits a peak gain of 6.3 dB and a triple-resonance at 6.72 GHz, 9.03 GHz and 10.31 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Topologies of Fourth-order Waveguide Quasi-elliptic Filter Based on the Singlets
abstract: This paper analyzes the different topologies of a fourth-order filter. Based on the high-order mode resonators (singlet), a quasi-elliptic filter response can be realized. But the existence of other high-order spurious modes will generate parasitic passbands, thus deteriorating the stopband level. To illustrate the influence brought by the spurious modes, mode analysis is introduced and the simulation results of four typical topologies are presented in order to get some useful design guidelines.

articleTitle: Single-Layer High-Efficiency Reflectarray Antenna Utilizing Half-Cut Elements
abstract: This paper develops a high-efficiency single-layer reflectarray antenna (RA) using the half-cut elements. Based on the half-cut method, the periodic size of the original element has been reduced by about 42.9%. Therefore, the same aperture of the array can accommodate more half-cut elements when compared with the original elements. Finally, the ability to compensate for the phase is enhanced and the aperture efficiency is improved. The proposed RA with a square aperture of 84x84 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is designed, fabricated, and tested. The experimental results realize a maximum gain of 27.48 dBi at 31 GHz, corresponding to an aperture efficiency as high as 59.12%. Besides, the 1-dB gain drop bandwidth of 15.3% (29.6 GHz - 34.5 GHz) is realized.

articleTitle: A 0.3-7.7GHz Noise-Canceling Low-Noise Amplifier in 55nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a broadband noise-canceling (NC) low-noise amplifier (LNA). The designed LNA adopts the common-gate (CG) common-source (CS) structure with active feedforward to improve the noise and power gain. Dual complementary pMOS-nMOS configuration is applied to act as the auxiliary amplifier, supplied by the current bleeding circuit. The simulated results show the proposed LNA features a gain of 7.6-10.6dB, noise figure (NF) of 2.84-3.56dB, and a -3dB bandwidth of 0.3-7.7GHz. It consumes 9.3mW from a 1.2V supply and occupies an area of 0.264mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: An Improved Robin Transmission Condition for Non-overlapping Domain Decomposition Method
abstract: An improved Robin transmission condition for non-overlapping domain decomposition method (IRTC-DDM) is proposed. The solution of subdomain problems converges very slowly to the solution of the original global problem by using traditional iterative method, when the medium properties on both sides of the subdomain interface are different. In order to accelerate the convergence, a new iterative strategy is applied. For closed domain transmission structures such as waveguides, numerical examples demonstrate that the results obtained by the proposed approach are in good agreement with the original solution. Compared with the traditional iterative method, the proposed approach has a faster convergence rate of 32.4%.

articleTitle: Synthesis of In-Between Microwave Filters with Complex Reflection Zeros
abstract: This paper reviews the use of complex reflection zeros (CRZs) in synthesis process to achieve “in-between” filters with additional benefits in physical implementation. CRZs bring more flexibilities to enable the satisfaction of physical constraints of diverse non-conventional filter topologies. With the added CRZs, the filters will present non-ideal in-between responses deviating from standard filter functions. Three applications of CRZs are reviewed: generalized strongly coupled resonator triplet (GSCRT) filters, inline extracted-zero filters, and inline path filters. Their in-between responses are analyzed and compared to guide a trade-off between electrical performance and physical layout.

articleTitle: SiO2-Based High-Gain Millimeter-Wave Transmitarray Antenna
abstract: A flat millimeter-wave transmitarray with a three-layer element is investigated in this paper. The proposed element can provide 360° phase coverage with a transmission coefficient better than -3 dB at 160 GHz. Then a transmitarray based on the element is designed with a focal-to-diameter ratio of 0.69, illuminated by a pyramidal horn antenna connected with WR-05 waveguide. The transmitarray is fabricated using the microfabrication technology based on SiO2 substrates, and the measured results demonstrate the performances of the antenna, a peak gain of 24.9 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 23.2%. In general, the proposed transmitarray verifies the feasibility of the microfabrication technology and can provide an alternative solution for applications in millimeter-wave systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Arc-Chord Approximation Demodulation Based on Green's Theorem
abstract: The continuous-wave (CW) radar has attracted many research interests in displacement motion sensing. To avoid interference from direct current (DC) offset, we propose the arc-chord approximation algorithm based on Green's theorem to realize immunity to DC offset. This method can obtain the target's direction of movement by using Green's theorem to calculate the area of the polygon. The theory and simulation show that the proposed arc-chord approximation algorithm based on Green's theorem effectively eliminates the coupling caused by the direct current offset and performs well compared to traditional methods at a low signal-to-noise ratio or when the I/Q trajectory spans across a semi-circle.

articleTitle: A novel multiple-model estimation algorithm based on Shannon Entropy
abstract: The conventional multiple-model (MM) estimation algorithms combing with radar sensor achieve great success in radar sensing. To obtain a satisfactory performance on state estimation, the fixed model set always has a large number of models. Thus, those algorithms hold the burden computational complexities, and can not guarantee the accuracy. In this paper, a new algorithm is proposed to overcome this issue. First, a reliable selection criteria, Shannon Entropy, is presented for MM algorithm. Furthermore, using the new election criteria, a novel multiple-model estimation fusion based on Shannon Entropy (MM-SE) is proposed to parallel and correct estimation probabilities of models. Simulation results highlight the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Compact Huygens' Metasurface for Orbital Angular Momentum Generation
abstract: Huygens' metasurface provides powerful method to designing high-efficiency meta-devices via balancing the electric/magnetic responses at the interface. However, most of the previously reported works operate in the transmission mode, leaving the reflection property to be unexploited. In this paper, a novel miniaturized reflective Huygens' meta-atom and metasurface is proposed. It comprises one vertically placed modified split resonant ring resonator (MSRR) and one planar terminally-bent electric dipole resonator (TBEDR), which provides the required magnetic and electric responses for constructing the Huygens resonance, respectively. Through judiciously adjustment on the key structural parameters, nearly full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi$</tex> reflection phase coverage is easily fulfilled together with high reflectance. As proof-of-concept demonstration, a high-efficiency reflective OAM generator is designed and simulated, and a good coincidence is witnessed between the simulation results and the design goals. The proposed work with merits of high-efficiency, compact size can be competitive candidate for the six-generation (6G) wireless communication system.

articleTitle: An 18-40Hz GaN Power Amplifier MMIC Utilizing Passive and Active Matching
abstract: A K-/Ka-band power amplifier (PA) MMIC, fabricated with an advanced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15\mu \mathrm{m} \ \text{GaN}$</tex> HEMT technology process, is developed and evaluated for multioctave operation in this paper. The impedance position of the transistor is accurately controlled by the combination of passive and active matching circuit. The ultra-wideband (UWB) P A demonstrates a power added efficiency (PAE) of 19% to 27% with a saturated power gain of 17 dB and an output power of 40.7-43 dBm from 18 to 40GHz at a drain voltage of 20V at 1ms pulse width with 10% duty cycle. The chip dimension is 3.7mm x 4.4 mm (16.28 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: Design of Cascaded Millimeter Wave Radar for Concealed Item Imaging
abstract: In this paper a 12-transmitter, 16-receiver cascaded millimeter-wave(mmWave) radar is designed for scenarios such as concealed item imaging and damage detection. The designed cascaded radar has 12 transmit antennas and 16 receive antennas, forming a virtual antenna array with 192 antenna elements. The cascaded radar is sampled in space by the movement of a two-axis motorized rail for two-dimensional (2-D) image reconstruction of metal items hidden under clothing, plastic, and packaging. The cascaded radar system extends the antenna array, and shortens the imaging scanning time, which has great potential in complex security inspection applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Mode Compact Multilayer Quasi-Elliptical SIW Filter
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual-band filter by vertically stacking three dual-mode substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW) cavities. With a fully enclosed cavity, by using the TE101 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{201}$</tex> modes, a compact dual-band filter with a controllable frequency ratio is achieved. To improve the selectivity, the filter is configured with four transmission zeros (TZs) nearby the passband with good symmetry through cross coupling. The filter's size is only 0.61 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{d}\times 1.15\lambda_{d}$</tex>, and the measured in-band minimum insertion loss is 0.92 and 1.45 dB for the first and second bands, respectively. The proposed filter shows the merits of a miniaturized size, low insertion loss, high selectivity, and good out-of-band suppression.

articleTitle: Free-Positioning Multi-Receiver Wireless Power Transfer System Based on Metasurface
abstract: Free-positioning and multi-user supportive wireless power transfer systems represent the next-generation technology for wireless charging of compact electronic devices. Here a metasurface for a free-positioning multi-receiver wireless power transfer system operating at the frequency of 6.78 MHz is proposed and numerically studied. Power transfer efficiency to a single receiver located in the center of the metasurface reaches 90%. We numerically demonstrate a high robustness of the proposed WPT system to the displacement of the receiver over the transmitter. At any free position of the receiver, the simulated power transfer efficiency is higher than 77%. We also numerically confirm the ability of simultaneous charging of two receivers on the metasurface. In this case, the overall efficiency remains high and reaches 91 % However, we note that the distribution of transferred power between the receivers is uneven and depends on their specific location and the coupling coefficient with the metasurface.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Stage Rectifier with Ultrawide Input Power Range
abstract: An ultrawide input power range rectifier is proposed in this paper. It is a three-stage rectifier containing three diodes with different characteristics. The main branch includes a diode with the lowest threshold voltage while the diodes with medium and high threshold voltage are located in the subbranches. By combining these three branches, the proposed rectifier is able to achieve high power conversion efficiency (PCE) within an ultrawide input power range. Two rectifiers prototype operating at 2.4 GHz are designed and simulated. The results show that the conversion efficiency of the two rectifiers is higher than 40% within the input range from -7 to 34.5 dBm and-14 to 26.8 dBm respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Filtering Folded Transmitarray Antenna Through Exploiting Its Main Reflectarray
abstract: A filtering folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) is presented for the first time through exploiting its main reflectarray in this paper. A high frequency-selective polarization conversion reflective surface (PCRS) is used as the main reflectarray of proposed filtering FTA design instead of conventional wideband polarization conversion reflective surface. The periodic element of frequency-selective bandpass PCRS is mainly composed of a rectangular ring and the metallic ground. A polarization conversion reflection zero can be introduced in the PCRS design by the coupling effect of the degenerated resonance of the dual-mode rectangular ring. It is easy to flexibly adjust the position of polarization conversion reflection zero to be at the upper or lower stopband of the PCRS. For the verification of the proposed filtering FTA design method, a prototype antenna has been presented as an example with its center frequency of 30GHz. Good filtering performance of the proposed antenna could be observed in the simulated results, which verifies the proposed filtering FTA design method.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Based Flat Lens for Beam Shaping
abstract: This paper introduces a metamaterial-based flat lens working in the microwave field. The lens can convert a Gaussian incident beam into a flat-top beam to mimic the function of a beam shaper. Unlike traditional dielectric beam shapers, the refractive index of metamaterial lenses can vary radially, so the lens profile is flat, and the thick-ness of the lens is thin. The metamaterial cell comprises a square metal patch and a dielectric substrate. Finally, the simulation results verify the feasibility of the theory.

articleTitle: Design of Wide-Angle Scanning Vivaldi Antenna Array for Satellite Communication
abstract: A 1 X 8 wide-angle scanning Vivaldi antenna for satellite communication phased array system is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is formed by a feed microstrip line terminated by a fan-shaped microstrip line on the top layer and a conical slot terminated by a circular slot notch on the bottom layer. In order to facilitate the connection with the phased array transceiver module, the antenna feed network is designed. Measured results show that the reflection coefficient is lower than -15 dB (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leqslant 1.45$</tex>) and the gain of antenna element is 3.5dB. The Vivaldi array achieves good beam scanning performance within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex>, which is suitable for satellite communication phased array system.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Gap Waveguide Technology Using EBG Composed of Parallel Grooves and Glide-Symmetric Semicircular-Holes
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel EBG structure to fabricate low-cost gap waveguides (GWs). The proposed unit cell of EBG structure consists of a pair of parallel shallow grooves with the glide-symmetric semicircular holes distributed laterally along the grooves, all positioned on the upper and lower metal layers. The much-reduced milling depth of the proposed EBG structure contributes to the advantage of efficient and low-cost manufacturing process. Besides, the proposed EBG can be more easily conformal with GWs within a compact feeding network because of the flexibly adaptable grooves and holes. As a proof of concept, both straight and side-by-side GWs are designed and measured to investigate the low-loss and high-isolation features of GWs exploiting the proposed EBG.

articleTitle: A 26-GHz CMOS Power Amplifier with Sea-of-Gates Transistor Layout and Systematic Modeling Techniques
abstract: A 26-GHz CMOS power amplifier is designed with sea-of-gates transistor layout to improve matching for phased array applications. A systematic modeling technique is proposed and verified to develop the hybrid model for high-frequency simulations. The power amplifier achieves a peak gain of 20 dB with a 9.2-GHz −3-dB bandwidth. At 26 GHz, it can offer a saturated output power of 13 dBm with a peak power added efficiency of 27%. The measured and simulated results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Accurate Heart Rate Estimation Based on Multi-Channel Cross-Correlation with a 60-GHz FMCW Radar
abstract: Radar-based vital sign monitoring has excellent potential for future telemedicine and intelligent aging. However, it is still difficult to estimate heart rate accurately at low signal-to-noise levels. In this work, a novel multi-channel cross-correlation algorithm based on single-input-multi-output (SIMO) frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is proposed for accurate heart rate estimation. The multi-channel cross-correlation algorithm can extract the periodic components (caused by heartbeat) from the chest displacement and suppress the non-periodic noise, thus enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the heart rate spectrum. The experimental results show that the multi-channel cross-correlation algorithm proposed in this paper can still estimate heart rate accurately when the conventional heart rate extraction algorithm fails to work.

articleTitle: A 5–6 GHz CMOS RF Front-End Module for FTTR Application
abstract: This paper presents a 5–6 GHz RF front-end module (FEM) integrating a power amplifier (PA), a low-noise amplifier (LNA), and a T/R switch. The proposed switch enables the matching network of the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx) to reuse the transformer and capacitor. Meanwhile, the PMOS switch is re-used to compensate for the AM-PM distortion of the PA. The compact layout minimizes the parasitics and optimizes the switching time. The chip is fabricated in a 55-nm CMOS process. Measurement results show that the high and low gain variation of Rx/Tx at 5–6 GHz is greater than 10 dB. The measured noise figure (NF) of Rx is less than 4.0 dB in high-gain mode (including the T/R Switch and off-mode PA). The measured output power 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) of Tx is better than 11.55 dBm (including the T/R Switch and off-mode LNA). The error vector magnitude (EVM) of the Tx is better than -35 dB at 0 dBm output power with 80-MHz 256-QAM orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal. The switching time of the Tx/Rx is less than 112 ns. The chip area of FEM is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.12\times 0.15\text{mm}^{2}$</tex> excluding I/O pads.

articleTitle: Microstrip Line to Waveguide Inline Transition for MMIC Integration
abstract: This paper presents a wideband inline transition from microstrip line (MSL) to rectangular waveguide (RWG). The usage of the bow-tie antenna can achieve wideband matching with the RWG, as well as a compact inline transition structure. In order to lift the restrictions of the substrate widths in conventional probes, the perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) packaging concept is used in this paper, resulting in a better integration ability with the monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC). A millimeter wave single transition is designed, simulation results show that the return loss is better than 15dB and the insertion loss is less than 0.97 dB from 106 to 180 GHz.

articleTitle: A 17-33GHz 6-bit Vector-Sum Phase Shifter with Wideband All-Pass I/Q Generator using an LC Compensation Network in 28-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced wideband all-pass I/Q generator using an LC compensation network, which mitigates the impact of the loading capacitance of Gilbert vector summer in a wideband phase shifter. A 17–33 GHz 6-bit vector- sum phase shifter (VSPS) is designed and implemented in 28-nm CMOS technology, which achieves a maximum average insertion loss of 2dB, <0.5dB root means square (RMS) gain error, and 0.2~1.65° RMS phase error over the operation bandwidth. The power consumption of the VSPS is 12mW with a core size of 0.16 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Broadband Metasurface Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
abstract: A miniaturized broadband metasurface (MTS) antenna based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is designed in this paper, which can be applied to modern wireless communication systems. The MTS consists of 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4$</tex> slotted rectangular patches, with a coplanar waveguide structure employed to excite the MTS. The antenna achieves miniaturization and broadband performance by slotting each patch at equal spacing and exciting the resonant modes of the MTS and the coplanar waveguide slot simultaneously. To validate the design, the proposed MTS antenna is simulated, fabricated, and tested. Measurement results indicate that the antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 48.5 % for reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leqslant-10\text{dB}$</tex>, with an overall size of 0.47 λ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{0}\times$</tex> 0.44λ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{0}\times$</tex> 0.07λ0, where λ0 is the free-space wavelength of 6.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Communication Channel of OAM Waves Through an Annular Aperture
abstract: Radio waves carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) have been used in the wireless communication for the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) application due to the OAM mode orthogonality. However, many fundamental properties like the channel performance of OAM waves penetrating through specific apertures are still missing in press. Hence, this paper investigates the OAM wave based channel through an annular slot aperture in an infinite perfect conductive wall. The far field radiation patterns of OAM beams are observed before and after the annular slot aperture, which have significant changes. The electrical fields around the aperture are also visualized to understand the OAM wave penetration, indicating that the OAM phase distribution is still maintained after the annular aperture, so as to the OAM mode orthogonality. A full wave analysis of the OAM wave channel is configured using uniform circular arrays of eight dipoles for each transmitting and receiving arrays. The investigation operating at 3.5 GHz reveals that the OAM receiver can still obtain very good mode isolation under the variation of the annular aperture sizes. Furthermore, multiple receiving arrays allocated simultaneously after the aperture both able to receive corresponding OAM modes properly, paving a way for multiple-input OAM array to multiple-output OAM arrays, offerina an additional degree of freedom for MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reshaping of an Open-Circuited Bidirectional Leaky-Wave Antenna
abstract: In this work, a method of reshaping the radiation pattern of an open-circuited EH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-mode bidirectional leaky-wave antenna is presented. Initially, it is found that an off-broadside radiation pattern is generated from the open-circuited EH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-mode bidirectional leaky-wave antenna. This is due to that several pairs of opposite magnetic currents exist on the antenna aperture. Afterwards, the opposite magnetic currents are reshaped to be with the same directions by introducing the microstrip EH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-mode component properly. Such a way, a single high-gain beam can be generated at broadside. The operation principles of the presented hybrid-mode unit are investigated by analyzing its electric-field distributions. Finally, a prototype containing 4 hybrid-mode units is practically implemented. The simulation and measurement both indicate that the original off-broadside radiation pattern is well reshaped to the desired single high-gain beam at broadside.

articleTitle: Excitation of TE11 Mode in Microwave Communication for Downhole While Drilling
abstract: In this paper, the excitation of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l l</inf> mode which is suitable in the downhole for gas drilling with high velocity gas flow is proposed. The proposed structure exploit two symmetrical loops which stretches from the aperture of the circular waveguide and connected to the inner wall of the waveguide. The simulation of the proposed excitation shows that the insertion loss is above −3.2 dB and the return loss is less than −15 dB from 2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz. Then, the equivalent circuit of the excitation is established to explain the working mechanism. Good agreement of the S parameters is observed between the electromagnetic simulation and the circuit model. Finally, the comparison of the stress between the proposed structure and the probe is made using fluid-structure interaction analysis. The maximum stress of the proposed structure is 0.047 MPa while that of the probe is 0.31 MPa.

Author Keywords: microwave communication for downhole while drilling

articleTitle: Wide-stopband, Low-loss and Self-packaged SISL Bandpass Filter Based on Capacitively Loaded Patch Resonators
abstract: A new type of capacitively loaded patch resonator (CLPR) is proposed in this letter to design wide-stopband, low-loss, self-packaged bandpass filters (BPFs) in substrate integrated suspended Line (SISL) platform. It has been shown that the introduction of capacitively loaded patch can introduce a new <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{00}$</tex> mode, which can be resonant at a quiet low frequency below the traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{01}(TM_{10})$</tex> mode in patch resonators. Consequently, the resonators' size will be smaller, and the performance will be wide-stop. Simultaneously, the radiation loss of the suggested BPF has been greatly decreased by the completely packed model developed by the SISL platform, resulting in a reasonably high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> factor. A BPF operating at 3.55 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 5.00% is constructed, simulated, and tested to confirm the theory behind new type patch resonators. When compared to a conventional rectangular patch resonator with the same center frequency, a size reduction of about 67% is seen.

articleTitle: A Simplified Digital Predistortion Model for Fully-Connected Hybrid Beamforming Massive MIMO Transmitters Using Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization Technique
abstract: In this paper, a pruning method using discrete particle swarm optimization (DPSO) is proposed to reduce the complexity of digital predistortion (DPD) for fully-connected (FC) hybrid beamforming (HBF) transmitters. In the DPSO algorithm, the position of each particle corresponds to a subset of model terms, and the subset that maximizes the model accuracy will be found through the cooperation between different particles. A simulation on a 4-stream 64-element FC HBF array is carried out, where the coefficients in each DPD model are reduced by approximately 50% while adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) and normalized mean square error (NMSE) remain almost unchanged.

articleTitle: An Improved Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Method Using Atomic Norm Minimization Algorithm Based on Support Set of Sparse Vectors
abstract: The compressed sensing-based direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method with high precision and fewer snapshots has garnered attention. However, existing studies decrease in accuracy significantly as the number of sources increases. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved DOA estimation method based on a support set of the sparse vector with an Atomic Norm Minimization (ANM) algorithm. The method constructs a support set of the sparse vector to enhance the sparse support degree. Then, the ANM algorithm is performed on the support set of the sparse vector to obtain DOA estimation results. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves the performance of DOA estimation compared to the classic ANM algorithm, particularly when the sparsity approaches or exceeds the number of array elements.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Oblique 45° Line Polarization Tightly Coupled Phased Array Antenna
abstract: In this paper, an oblique 45° linear polarization close-coupled antenna unit operating from 2GHz to 18GHz is designed. The standing wave of the antenna unit in the working frequency band is less than 2.2, the tight coupling structure between the units effectively expands the antenna bandwidth, the middle consumable block film structure can effectively suppress the resonance point in the frequency band, introduce a short route and lumped resistance between the antenna vibrator arm and the ground, strengthen the suppression effect of the resonance in the band, and the existence of parasitic patches can improve the loss of the unit at a large angle. On the basis of the antenna unit, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> closely coupled antenna array is designed, and most of the standing waves of the array are less than 3 in the 2GHz-18GHz operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Design of Bandstop Frequency-Selective Structure Based on Corrugated Structure
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design of bandstop frequency-selective structure with ultra-wide stopband based on corrugated structure. The proposed three-dimensional (3-D) structure is a periodic structure composed of narrow metal strip lines printed on regular triangular prisms. The effects of structural parameters on stopband performance are investigated. The simulation results show that the -10 dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of stopband is 80%, and the angular stability of the structural response is up to 60 degrees for both TE and TM polarization. Moreover, the period of the corrugated structure is 0.2λ, and the thickness along the wave propagation is 0.26λ.

articleTitle: Study on Weighted K-Nearest Neighbors Indoor Location Algorithm Based on Random Forest Access Point Selection
abstract: The conventional approach to determining fingerprint location is susceptible to errors induced by indoor small-scale fading, this shortcoming leads to a greater propensity for inaccuracy. In this study, we propose a novel Weighted K-Nearets Neighbors (WKNN) indoor location algorithm, which capitalizes on the benefits of random forest optimization (RF-WKNN). The primary advantage of this algorithm is its ability to leverage the random forest algorithm to classify the positioning base stations that have been pre-selected. This technique serves to mitigate the influence of received signal strength (RSS) in the presence of small-scale fading. In addition, we have conducted tests using 2.4GHz and 5GHz WIFI signals. The results of these tests reveal that the proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional WKNN algorithm by a margin of 6.5%.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz Wide-Angle Scanning Planar Phased Array Antenna in Triangular Lattice
abstract: A 60 GHz wide-scanning planar triangular-lattice phased array based on magnetoelectric (ME) dipole element is presented in this paper. The parasitic patches are introduced to the two sides of the ME dipole to strengthen the radiation in low-elevation region so as to broaden its half power beam width (HPBW). The simulated results shows that the proposed antenna element possesses a 3-dB beamwidth of over 110° in the two planes within the operating frequency band of 59–64 GHz. Based on this antenna element, an eight-element phased array in triangular grid arrangement is designed and simulated. As results, the main beam can scan from -60° to 60° in both E- and If-planes, and the maximum gain of the antenna array is 15 dBi when the beam points to the boresight. The proposed planar phased array is very potential to applied in V -band wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A 6-Bit E-band Vector-Sum Phase Shifter With Transformer-Based Hybrid in 65nm CMOS
abstract: In this paper, a 6-Bit E-band vector-sum phase shifter based on a 65 nm CMOS process is proposed. A transformer- based fully differential hybrid is designed to generate high-precision orthogonal signals, which presents a compact layout and effectively widens the operating bandwidth. Besides, a low phase invariance technique is applied to variable gain amplifiers (VGAs). The measurement results exhibit that the proposed circuit achieves a 360° phase shifting range with 5.625° step in the wideband from 69 GHz to 81 GHz. The root-mean-square (RMS) phase error is only 1.17° at the center frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), and the RMS amplitude error is less than 1.2dB. Thanks to the proposed quadrature generator, the core area of the phase shifter is 500×240 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-Octave PA Using a Double Optimization Methodology
abstract: In this work, a double optimization algorithm is used to design a multi-octave power amplifier (PA). The initial PA is de-signed based on Chebyshev low-pass topology. The advanced de-sign system (ADS) embedded optimization technique is used to ob-tain a good starting point for Bayesian optimization (BO), and then BO method is carried out to further optimize the performance of the designed PA. Finally, a multi-octave PA with the output power of more than 40 dBm and power added efficiency (PAE) of better than 60% in the band of 0.7-3.1 GHz is obtained.

articleTitle: A Low-profile Wide Band Planar Antenna Based on Multimode Resonance
abstract: In the sub-6G age, communication requires higher bandwidth for antennas. A low-profile wideband antenna based on multimode resonance has been created. By etching two slots on the rectangular patch, an additional resonance can be excited. The bandwidth and reflection coefficients of the antenna have been significantly improved by connecting a secondary radiation patch to the main radiator, consisting of two metal arms and connecting lines. Compared with traditional wideband antennas, the proposed antenna is compact and has a simpler structure. Finally, the proposed antenna was fabricated and tested to verify this design. The measured and simulated results are highly consistent, demonstrating a wide bandwidth of 19% and an average gain of 8.1dBi.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Utilizing Hybrid Configuration
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized bandpass filter (BPF) exploiting the hybrid eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW) and microstrip-line (MSL) structures. A second-order EMSIW BPF with corner-feed type is exhibited first. In order to enhance the performance of the prototype, two MSL resonators are integrated into two EMSIW cavities to achieve a fourth-order BPF without extra circuit size. Three transmission zeros (TZs) are introduced at the right side of the operating passband. To validate the designed concept, a prototype is thoroughly fabricated and measured. Reasonable agreement has been approached between the simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Investigation of Bending Losses for the PTFE Dielectric Waveguide in the Sub-THz band
abstract: In this work, the bending performance of a solid cir-cular polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) dielectric waveguide with a 1.5 mm diameter is studied in the sub-THz band. Simulations and measurements of the 90° bending PTFE dielectric waveguides are carried out with 5/10/30 mm bending radii and the dominant HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>mode under two orthogonal polarizations, and the investigated frequency band ranges from 88 to 140 GHz. The simulated and measured results can generally agree with each other, and the measured bending losses with a 5 mm bending radius are 0.5-7.8 dB with vertical polarized HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>mode and 1.9-13.2 dB with hori-zontal polarized HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>mode, respectively. In particular, the bending loss can be neglected when the radius is larger than 30 mm and the frequency is higher than 120 GHz, and adopting the polarization orthogonal to the bending direction can also decrease the bending loss. This investigation is helpful in the applications of the PTFE dielectric waveguide in the sub-THz band.

articleTitle: Fast Prediction Method for PIM Distribution on Waveguide Temperature Compensation Structure Using DC Non-Linearity Diagnosis
abstract: This paper proposes a fast prediction method for PIM distribution in the waveguide resonator with temperature compensation (TC) structure. When faced with temperature changes, the waveguide filters expand or contract, affecting the size-dependent resonant frequency. Therefore, filters with high selectivity necessitate temperature compensation structures to ensure thermal stability under stringent circumstances, especially in space applications. Structural connections and contacts always exist in the TC structures, serving as typical sources of passive intermodulation (PIM). When compensation appears, the mechanical deformation accompanying thermal stress will complicate the PIM analysis. DC non-linearity diagnosis is applied in this proposed method, which can fast predict the PIM distribution in TC structures without the PIM test. This prediction method can significantly cut off the testing cost and attain high efficiency in PIM analysis.

articleTitle: A Fully Integrated GaN Doherty Power Amplifier for WLAN 802.11ax Application
abstract: In this paper, a fully integrated GaN Doherty power amplifier for WLAN 802.11ax application is presented. The output match network is realized by T-type three microline to decrease insert loss and increase efficiency. The PA is fabricated in a 0.25um GaN HEMT technology with a die size of 2.7mm*2mm. The DPA is designed at 6.4~7.2 GHz with a 28V supply voltage. The DPA can obtain a large signal gain over 20dB, >30% DE at 10-dB PBO, an ACPR of -27.7 dBc without DPD, and -52.37 dBc with DPD at an average output power of 27 dBm with a 100 MHz 64-QAM modulation signal.

articleTitle: A Simple Probe-fed Ultrawideband Patch Antenna with Annular Gap
abstract: In this paper, a simple and single-layer probe-fed ul-trawideband (UWB) microstrip patch antenna with an annular gap at the X band and Ku band is proposed. The annular gap is used to compensate for the inductance caused by the probe-fed by introducing a capacitor value. The influence of antenna parame-ters on performance is analyzed thoroughly. Prototypes are de-signed, simulated, fabricated, and measured to verify the proposed UWB patch antenna. The simulated and measured results demon-strate that the proposed UWB patch antenna possesses the merit of wide operating bandwidth (up to 52%), and the maximum and minimum gains are 7.44 dBi at 9.19 GHz and 3.5 dBi at 13.06 GHz, respectively, which provides a foundation for the applications in broadband scenarios.

articleTitle: High-Order Harmonic Mixing based Ultra-Low-Cost L-Band GNSS Signal Generator
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-cost L-band spread spectrum GNSS signal generator. Conventional SDR-based GNSS signal generators are expensive and they require a standalone computer to generate the baseband signal. The pro-posed ultra-low-cost GNSS signal generator adopts high-order harmonic mixing techniques to greatly simplify the LO chain design and uses an I2S peripheral on the micro controller to gen-erate the spread spectrum signal stream. Due to the extremely lean architecture, the entire system contains only 3 active devices and is fairly low-cost. A novel bit operation-based 1-bit quantization method is proposed to generate the required bitstream.

articleTitle: A 140 GHz LTCC-based High-efficiency Heterogeneous Reflectarray Antenna
abstract: One design strategy of heterogeneous reflectarray antenna (RA) is presented. A 140 GHz high-efficiency low-profile RA based on heterogeneous reflective elements is designed, fabricated and measured. Compared with homogeneous RA, the proposed heterogeneous RA shows better directionality, higher aperture efficiency, wider gain-bandwidth and lower cross-polarization. The measured results of the proposed RA indicate the realized gain of 31.39 dBi at 140 GHz and aperture efficiency of 46.22%. With above features, the proposed RA is expected to use for short distance communication applications in THz band.

articleTitle: A X/Ka-Band Low-Profile Double-Conical-Beams Antenna with Vortex Electromagnetic Waves
abstract: Antennas with conical beams have the advantage in anti-interference applications. This paper proposes a low-profile antenna with two conical beams working at X and Ka bands. To save space, a Ka-band multi-ring antenna composed of one circular plate and five concentric rings is placed on the center of an X-band uniform circular array (UCA) antenna formed by eight microstrip patches. A vortex electromagnetic wave (VEW) with mode 1 is generated with the UCA antenna with phase difference of the elements of 45 deg. With different phase difference, the higher modes of the VEW can be formed. The cylindrical cavity not only serves as the cavity of the Ka-band antenna, but also physically separates the two antennas which makes them do not interference with each other. The peak gain at 37.5GHz of Ka band is 12.4dBi, and the 3dB beamwidth is in the range of 6.9-24.4deg. The peak gain at 10GHz of X band is 8.2dBi, and the 3dB beamwidth is in the range of 12.8-43deg.

articleTitle: A 59–65 GHz Frequency Generator Based on 20 GHz VCO and Tripler with Low Phase Noise and Low Power Consumption in 40-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper proposes a 59–65 GHz, 10.58<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> tuning range, -97.2 dBc/Hz@lMHz phase noise, 16 mW power consumption, 181.45 dBc/Hz@lMHz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FoM}_{\mathrm{T}}$</tex>, 0.052 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>area frequency generator based on 20 GHz VCO and multiplied-by-three frequency multiplier with the technology of 40-nm and 1.1 V supply voltage. The major idea is to construct a 20 GHz VCO with good phase noise and use the theory of injection lock to attain 60 GHz output. Switching capacitors and stacked MOSFETs are used in VCO, and a fourth-order resonator is applied in the multiplier.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Rectifying Surface with Flexible DC Output Connection Structure for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper proposed an efficient electromagnetic rectifying surface array at 5.8 GHz. This rectifying surface can achieve impedance matching with free space by optimizing its geometry. Consequently, this rectifying surface can achieve efficient capture of ambient electromagnetic energy. Diodes can achieve the rectification and synthesis of the captured energy. In this work, diodes is directly connect to the energy-capturing surface which can reduce the insertion loss and complexity of this rectifying surface. It is worth noting that diodes are behind the substrate which can avoid the interference of incident energy on energy rectifying. The output voltage of this rectifying surface can be controlled by changing the synthesis mode of DC energy. The simulation results shows that this rectifying surface has the energy capturing efficiency of 99.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and energy conversion efficiency of 79.8%.

articleTitle: Flexible and Small-size Graphene Ultrawideband Antenna with Wi-MAX/WLAN Dual-band Suppression Characteristics
abstract: In our work, a flexible, small-size ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna based on a high conductive graphene assembly film (GAF) with dual-band suppression characteristics in the WiMAX/WLAN band is proposed. The proposed antenna is only 23x22x1.024 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in size and by 50 R coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed. Band suppression characteristics are acquired by adding two complementary split ring resonators (CSRR). It operates in the 2.8-9.65 GHz band, with the suppressed bands of WiMAX (3.3-3.8 GHz) and WLAN (5.15-5.85 GHz). The UWB antenna is made of flexible material, which can maintain excellent resonance characteristics under different bending conditions. Also, making the same type of copper antenna for comparison, the GAF antenna has broadband advantage at mid and high freuuencies,

articleTitle: A Continuously Tunable Wilkinson Power Divider with a Flat Division Ratio
abstract: In this paper, a Wilkinson power divider with flat and continuously tunable division ratio is presented. A pair of adjustable networks are utilized to achieve a flat division ratio and good matching performance within a specific frequency range. Each network consists of two varactor diodes and three segments of transmission lines, which is equivalent to a quarter-wavelength transmission line with tunable characteristic impedance. By adjusting the capacitance of the varactor diodes, the equivalent electrical length of the network can be maintained at 90 degrees while its equivalent characteristic impedance is varied. For verification, a proposed power divider with a continuously tunable range of 3.2-5.8dB is designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: Beam Planning for Multiple Beam Antenna With Discrete Coverage
abstract: A beam planning method for multiple beam antenna has been presented in this paper. For nonuniform discrete coverage, a available beam plan can be obtained speedily using the proposed method with backtracking algorithm. And from the results of beam plans of a large number of random samples, the optimal beam plan can be chosen, which have the minimal number of colors and the maximal minimum distance of beams with same color. Compared with the traditional manual beam planning which is time-consuming and difficult to get the optimal beam plan, the proposed method has overwhelming advantages.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Stereo Decoupled Quasi-Yagi Antenna Array by Using SRRs
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized stereo quasi-Yagi antenna array. When the distance between array elements is 0.16 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, the coupling is suppressed using the periodically ordered splitring resonators (SRRs). The simulation results indicate that the isolation of the decoupled antenna array at 2.4 GHz is increased by nearly four times, and the gain is almost unaffected. Meanwhile, the channel capacity of the suggested decoupled quasi-Yagi antenna array reaches 7.999 bps/Hz when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is 20 dB. The effectiveness of our suggested decoupling structure is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Range Migration Algorithm for Synthetic Aperture Radar Based on FPGA
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging systems are integral to the fields of civil security inspection and military warfare. However, these systems are limited by stringent constraints such as power consumption, volume, cost, and weight, leading to a reduction in their flexibility and applicability. To mitigate these challenges, a novel hardware implementation of the two-dimensional range migration algorithm (RMA) utilizing field-programmable gate arrays (FPGA) is proposed in this paper. The test results show that the system can process complex data of size 256×256 with data type of 32 bits in just 3.18ms at a clock frequency of 100MHz, which is about 1000 times faster than that with MATLAB while preserving the same image quality.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Dual-Channel T/R MMIC Based on a 0.18-μm GaAs E/D pHEMT Technology
abstract: Based on GaAs 0.18μm E/D pHEMT technology, a small size dual-channel transmitter and receiver (T/R) control chip was developed at Ku band. It contains two receiving channels and two transmitting channels, a power divider, series and parallel conversion and other functional units. For the first time, this high integrated multifunctional chip is with 48-bit series parallel converter, reducing the number of external interfaces. In addition, high precision numerical control (NC) phase shift and NC attenuation performance are realized by integrated collaborative design. Test results show that in the frequency band of 15 - 17 GHz, this chip has a gain greater than 2.1 dB in receiving state, input & output return loss less than −10 dB, phase-shift root mean square (RMS) errors of transmitting and receiving less than 2.3 and 2.4°, and attenuation RMS errors of transmitting and receiving less than 0.26 dB and 0.28 dB. The transmitting state gain is greater than 15.4 dB, the input and output return loss is less than −11 dB.

articleTitle: Synthesis Theory and Modeling of Guided Wave-based Three-Dimensional Frequency-Selective Structures
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis and design methods of the guided wave-based three-dimensional (3-D) narrowband and wideband bandpass frequency-selective structures (FSSs), which are employing three filtering networks and numerical short-open-load (SOL) technique-based modeling extraction method. To predict the filtering performance of the desired FSS in advance, the circuit parameters of the corresponding equivalent circuit model (ECM) or filtering network are first calculated according to the given specifications. Subsequently, the physical layout of FSS is modeled by mapping to the ECM. Finally, three prototypes are presented to validate the proposed design conception.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a Tunable Terahertz Absorber Based on Vanadium Dioxide Metamaterial
abstract: In this paper, a tunable terahertz absorber is demonstrated and experimentally verified, which is composed of a patterned vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) film and a metal reflector layer, separated by a quartz dielectric medium. A tunable absorptivity property of the absorber, revealed at frequencies of 0.5 THz and 0.85 THz, can be flexibly designed by manipulating the conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The simulated results show that, the absorptivity of 99.9% and 3.1 % can be achieved when the conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film at 30000 S/m and 100 S/m, respectively. A sample of the designed absorber prototype is manufactured under a micro-fabrication process and measured through a terahertz time-domain spectral system in free-space. The conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is manipulated by a thermostatic table, and the measured results verify the tunable absorptivity property of the absorber. This proposed prototype is an effective manner for tunable terahertz metamaterial absorbers, which has potential applications in the fields of sensor, military stealth, and energy harvesting.

articleTitle: A Wideband Analog Baseband with Accurate dB-Linear Characteristic in 40nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a wideband analog baseband (ABB) with accurate dB-linear characteristic in 40nm CMOS technology. The proposed ABB consists of a five-stage variable gain amplifier (VGA), a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order Butterworth filter, a DC-offset cancellation (DCOC) network, and an output buffer. The VGA provides dB-linear gain tuning while the filter provides sufficient out-of-band rejection. Active inductive load and active feedback are adopted to extend its bandwidth. Moreover, an approach that neutralizes dB-linear gain error is proposed. The simulation results show continuous gain tuning range from -10dB to 30dB with a gain error less than 0.3dB. Meanwhile, A bandwidth of 4.7 GHz is achieved for the entire gain range. The power consumption is 13mW from a 1 V supply, excluding the output buffer. The core circuit occupies an area of 0.056 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mm^{2}$</tex>

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of FSS Loaded Antennas Based on Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions
abstract: A fast analysis method based on the generalized sheet transition condition (GSTC) is proposed for frequency selective surface(FSS) loaded antennas in this paper. In this method, the physical structure of the FSS is replaced with its corresponding impedance surface to avoid extremely dense meshes in full-wave simulations. A FSS loaded low profile antenna is considered as an example to validate the efficiency and accuracy of the method. Numerical results demonstrate good agreement between the fast analysis method and the conventional full-wave simulations.
