It is also found that the number of meshes and the simulation time are significantly reduced in the proposed fast analysis method.

articleTitle: Retrieval Effective Electromagnetic Parameters of Honeycomb Absorbing Materials
abstract: In this paper, a method for extracting the effective parameters of honeycomb absorbing materials is proposed. The method in-volves transforming the honeycomb absorbing structure into a homogeneous slab of anisotropic material, based on reflection and transmission coefficients obtained at two incident angles and polarizations. Through the equivalent permittivity and permeability, the reflection and transmission at arbitrary incident angles can be calculated effectively. Analytical expressions are derived to retrieve the equivalent medium parameters. To demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the theory, the method is applied to simulate and predict results on a honeycomb absorbing composite. Furthermore, the mono static radar cross section (RCS) of a perfect electric conductor (PEC) plate covered with the honeycomb absorbing composites and the effective slab are calculated, the results demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A 12-Bit 125MSps Binary-Scaled Redundant SAR ADC with Partial Split Capacitor DAC
abstract: This paper introduces a 12-bit high-speed successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) 28nm CMOS process. Several techniques are proposed to improve analog-to-digital converter (ADC) performance. The binary scaling redundancy technique proposed in this paper can suppress the settling error of capacitor digital-to-analog converter (DAC) without sacrificing the resolution, thus reducing the settling time. Partial splitting capacitance technology can improve the conversion speed, and the dynamic offset can be reduced without the common mode voltage (Vcm) phase when the DAC is reset. In addition, the reference scaling binary method can exponentially reduce the number of unit capacitors, reduce power consumption and improve conversion speed without sacrificing accuracy. The ADC achieves an SFDR of 87.66dB and 11.68-bit ENOB with Nyquist input consuming 7.02mW at 0.9V supply, resulting in a Figure of merit (FoM) of 17.12fJ/conversion step.

articleTitle: A DC~67 GHz Memristive RF Switch Based on Conductive-Bridging RAM on High-Resistivity Silicon Substrate
abstract: A RF switch based on the conductive bridge random access memory (CBRAM) technique is proposed and fabricated on a high-resistivity silicon (HRS) substrate. The CBRAM-based switch can maintain its ON/OFF state without a continuous biasing, leading to ultralow power consumption potentially. Experimental and equivalent circuit results show the switch provides a relatively low ON-state insertion loss of less than 1.2 dB up to 67 GHz. The OFF-state isolation is over 10 dB. The retention and switching characteristics of the proposed memristive switch are tested. It is demonstrated that the baking process at 125°C has small impact on the ON/OFF-state resistances and the device can still be switched under the high temperature of 85°C.

articleTitle: Comparison of Digital Predistortion of GaN Power Amplifiers with Trapping Effects Under Different Bandwidth Signals
abstract: The degeneration of the power amplifiers (PA) with trapping effects under different type signals is investigated in this paper. A compensation model is built to compensate the trapping effects of the PA,. The experimental result shows that the stronger fluctuation of the trap state, the deeper trapping effects degeneration on the PA performance when a GaN Doherty is excited by signals with the discontinuous power level.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of Four-Pole Waveguide Filter Integrating Neural Networks and MOR-Based Rational Transfer Functions
abstract: Neuro-transfer function (neuro-TF) methods are increasingly applied in the parametric modeling of microwave passive devices. Current neuro-TF methods based on poles/residues have the problem of poles/residues discontinuity when the geometry varies widely, and neuro-TF methods based on poles/zeros form require specific algorithms for ordering or poles/zeros matching. The neuro-TF method based on rational transfer functions proposed in recent years solves the above three problems simultaneously. The purpose of this paper is to apply the MOR-based neuro-TF method with rational transfer function to model a four-pole waveguide filter.
